item.title: Bethesda’s Big Elder Scrolls Tease Quietly Reveals New Xbox Strategy
item.description: Both were more substantive than Bethesda's one-word-and-a-quote tease, if only a bit. They included impressive cinematic trailers and interviews with creatives. Diablo 5 even got some plot and game design details. But it was clear that we are a long way from seeing gameplay on either game, and the real shock was the announcement of far-off release dates: spring 2029 for Diablo 5 , 2030 for StarCraft .

item.title: Iran warns of wider war if US attacks after Trump election rout
item.description: Iran’s supreme leader warned on Wednesday that the Middle East war would widen if the US resumes its attacks, dismissing hopes of a policy shift in Washington after midterm elections dealt a blow to President Donald Trump. Trump has recently threatened to renew the war against Iran amid similar rhetoric from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but on Tuesday he suffered a resounding defeat in polls that will strip his Republicans of control over Congress. The results could constrain Trump’s ability to enact his agenda, though the president retains the power to order new strikes. “Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the United States can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken,” Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement Wednesday. He also warned that if the United States did choose further military action, the scope of the war would widen, without elaborating. Khamenei has yet to appear in public since he took power in March following the killing of his father and predecessor in US-Israeli strikes, and has communicated through written messages. Earlier, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, said Americans had voted against war in the midterms. “Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message,” he posted on X. “If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare,” Ghalibaf said. Iran’s judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been “defeated both militarily and politically”. The war has proved unpopular among the US public, who have seen the cost of living rise after a spike in energy prices caused by the war. Trump on Tuesday acknowledged the conflict may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party. “I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I’ve done,” Trump told Fox News. On Tuesday the US launched strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting five explosions in rapid succession. “They built an anti-aircraft facility… As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night very nicely,” Trump told US media, but he called it a “minor attack”. – ‘Locked and loaded’ – Earlier this week the president said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. However, he told the Financial Times newspaper on Tuesday that a full-scale resumption of war may not be necessary. “We seem to be getting everything we want,” he said. “I’m ready, we’re ready. item.content:encoded: Iran’s supreme leader warned on Wednesday that the Middle East war would widen if the US resumes its attacks, dismissing hopes of a policy shift in Washington after midterm elections dealt a blow to President Donald Trump. Trump has recently threatened to renew the war against Iran amid similar rhetoric from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, but on Tuesday he suffered a resounding defeat in polls that will strip his Republicans of control over Congress. The results could constrain Trump’s ability to enact his agenda, though the president retains the power to order new strikes. “Those who still harbour even the slightest hope that the behaviour of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts, or who imagine that making concessions to the United States can dissuade it from hostility towards the Iranian nation, are seriously mistaken,” Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement Wednesday. Khamenei has yet to appear in public since he took power in March following the killing of his father and predecessor in US-Israeli strikes, and has communicated through written messages. Earlier, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, said Americans had voted against war in the midterms. “Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message,” he posted on X. “If the US govt betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare,” Ghalibaf said. Iran’s judiciary chief Gholamhossein Mohseni Ejei also hailed the election results, saying Trump had been “defeated both militarily and politically”. The war has proved unpopular among the US public, who have seen the cost of living rise after a spike in energy prices caused by the war. Trump on Tuesday acknowledged the conflict may have played a part in the defeat of his Republican Party. “I think a part of it was Iran, but at the same time, people understood the importance of what I’ve done,” Trump told Fox News. On Tuesday the US launched strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, with Iranian state media reporting five explosions in rapid succession. “They built an anti-aircraft facility… As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night very nicely,” Trump told US media, but he called it a “minor attack”. – ‘Locked and loaded’ – Earlier this week the president said he still had to “take care” of one or two targets, including so-called Pickaxe Mountain in central Iran, a suspected nuclear site which Tehran denies is such a facility. However, he told the Financial Times newspaper on Tuesday that a full-scale resumption of war may not be necessary. “We seem to be getting everything we want,” he said. “I’m ready, we’re ready. We’re locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it.” The president’s remarks come with diplomatic efforts by mediators in full swing in an attempt to prevent any resumption of fighting. On Tuesday Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said his government was still trying to resolve the crisis through dialogue. Pezeshkian said Iran’s supreme leader had granted the government new powers to negotiate on issues previously off-limits. Qatar, a mediator in the protracted wrangling, said it remained hopeful of an interim deal. Both sides “are currently reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented”, Qatari foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari told reporters. China also said Wednesday that avoiding a return to hostilities was a top priority in its diplomatic efforts with the countries. The war, triggered in February when the US and Israel pummelled Iran in a massive wave of strikes, has been at a stalemate for months. Iranian officials have repeatedly warned of wide-ranging retaliation if Washington resumes the war. item.title: Step-by-step: How to download NIN slip online for free
item.description: The National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) has explained how Nigerians can download their National Identification Number (NIN) slips online for free through its NINAuth mobile application. The commission said the service allows registered NIN holders to obtain their official identification slips directly on their mobile phones without visiting NIMC enrolment centres or paying third-party agents. NIMC demonstrated the process in a video shared on its official X account on Wednesday, outlining the steps users must follow to access and download the document. According to the commission, Nigerians can obtain their NIN slips by completing a few steps on the NINAuth application. How to download your NIN slip using the NINAuth app NIN holders who wish to download their identification slips are required to follow these steps: Download the NINAuth application from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Open the application on your mobile phone. Tap the “Do More with NINAuth” option. Select “NIN Slip” from the available services. Complete the facial authentication process to verify your identity. Once authentication is successful, select “Download NIN Slip” to generate the document. Save the downloaded slip on your mobile phone for future use. NIMC explained that successful facial verification would allow users to access and download their official identification slips directly through the application. “Once verified, click on ‘Download NIN Slip’ to generate and save the official NIMC-issued NIN slip into your mobile phone,” the commission said. It described the service as a convenient and secure way for Nigerians to access their identification documents, stressing that the process was free. “It is that simple, it is free, available, and a few taps away. Get yours today,” NIMC added. What is a National Identification Number (NIN)? The National Identification Number is an 11-digit unique identification number issued by NIMC to Nigerians and legal residents following successful registration. It serves as a means of establishing and verifying an individual’s identity and links their personal records to the National Identity Database. The number is used for identity verification across several sectors, including banking, telecommunications, government services and other official transactions. Vanguard News The post Step-by-step: How to download NIN slip online for free appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Beauty particle’ decay opens the door to the zeptoverse
item.description: A detector in the LHCb experiment CERN Welcome to the zeptoverse , the world of the unprecedentedly small. A new analysis of data from the Large Hadron Collider has uncovered an extraordinarily rare particle decay that opens the door to this realm and its secrets. The standard model of particle physics tabulates all known particles and how they interact, but it cannot explain dark matter and dark energy, which fill most of our universe. Consequently, researchers test its predictions in particle collider experiments, searching for signs of new particles and forces. Read more We’re solving the fundamental mystery of how reality is glued together Now, Paula Collins and her colleagues at the Large Hadron Collider beauty (LHCb) experiment at CERN in Switzerland have found the first evidence of a rare decay involving the “beauty quark” particle, which opens a whole new world for these searches. Advertisement “People have been searching for it for more than 40 years,” she says. “Everyone’s just over the moon.” Beauty particles are often produced in the LHC’s particle smashes, but the researchers focused on a specific process where a beauty quark gets annihilated by an antiquark – its antimatter cousin – and their annihilation produces another particle and antiparticle pair, the electron-like muon and antimuon, which can be detected. This process is exceedingly rare and has eluded experiments for decades. Subscriber-only newsletter Sign up to Lost in Space-Time Sign up to newsletter “These very, very rare decays, they’re almost impossible according to the current laws of physics,” says team member Harry Cliff at the University of Cambridge. “This happens only for one in 10 billion beauty particles.” The finding is still preliminary, with relatively large uncertainties and a significance level of 3.2 sigma, while the gold standard for a discovery is 5 sigma. This means the chance that the signal in the experiment occurred randomly instead of being meaningful is about 0.3 per cent. Cliff says future experiments ought to lower this uncertainty, but the data already reveals that we have reached the zeptoverse, a world at scales as small as sextillionths of a metre – the smallest ever explored. Yet undiscovered denizens of this world could influence the beauty particle decay process and because the process is so rare, researchers would immediately spot that change, says Collins. In this way, measuring this process is like surveying the zeptoverse. Read more Unexpected hints of dark matter should breathe life into particle physics “It was really a surprise that the team would be able to see this very rare event,” says Jure Zupan at the University of Cincinnati in Ohio. He says this was made possible by technical upgrades that the LHCb team has made in recent years. “It’s like a very powerful microscope where now you’re able to see much shorter distances because you don’t have a fog in front of your eyes,” says Zupan. “It’s absolutely exciting,” says Zoltan Lig

item.content:encoded: A detector in the LHCb experiment CERN Welcome to the zeptoverse , the world of the unprecedentedly small. A new analysis of data from the Large Hadron Collider has uncovered an extraordinarily rare particle decay that opens the door to this realm and its secrets. The standard model of particle physics tabulates all known particles and how they interact, but it cannot explain dark matter and dark energy, which fill most of our universe. Consequently, researchers test its predictions in particle collider experiments, searching for signs of new particles and forces. Read more We’re solving the fundamental mystery of how reality is glued together Now, Paula Collins and her colleagues at the Large Hadron Collider beauty (LHCb) experiment at CERN in Switzerland have found the first evidence of a rare decay involving the “beauty quark” particle, which opens a whole new world for these searches. Advertisement “People have been searching for it for more than 40 years,” she says. “Everyone’s just over the moon.” Beauty particles are often produced in the LHC’s particle smashes, but the researchers focused on a specific process where a beauty quark gets annihilated by an antiquark – its antimatter cousin – and their annihilation produces another particle and antiparticle pair, the electron-like muon and antimuon, which can be detected. This process is exceedingly rare and has eluded experiments for decades. Subscriber-only newsletter Sign up to Lost in Space-Time Sign up to newsletter “These very, very rare decays, they’re almost impossible according to the current laws of physics,” says team member Harry Cliff at the University of Cambridge. “This happens only for one in 10 billion beauty particles.” The finding is still preliminary, with relatively large uncertainties and a significance level of 3.2 sigma, while the gold standard for a discovery is 5 sigma. This means the chance that the signal in the experiment occurred randomly instead of being meaningful is about 0.3 per cent. Cliff says future experiments ought to lower this uncertainty, but the data already reveals that we have reached the zeptoverse, a world at scales as small as sextillionths of a metre – the smallest ever explored. Yet undiscovered denizens of this world could influence the beauty particle decay process and because the process is so rare, researchers would immediately spot that change, says Collins. In this way, measuring this process is like surveying the zeptoverse. Read more Unexpected hints of dark matter should breathe life into particle physics “It was really a surprise that the team would be able to see this very rare event,” says Jure Zupan at the University of Cincinnati in Ohio. He says this was made possible by technical upgrades that the LHCb team has made in recent years. “It’s like a very powerful microscope where now you’re able to see much shorter distances because you don’t have a fog in front of your eyes,” says Zupan. “It’s absolutely exciting,” says Zoltan Ligeti at the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory in California. This process is not only ultra-rare but mathematical theories predict it very well so investigating it makes for a particularly important test of the standard model, says Cristina Lazzeroni at the University of Birmingham in the UK. The new measurement is consistent with the standard model, but Ligeti says this does not mean that all possible new particles have been ruled out. In his view, the new measurement implies that effects of such particles must be small but not necessarily negligible and LHCb could quantify this further going forward. “What they measured is very interesting, but I think even more interesting is the promise [of future experiments],” says Zupan. Cliff, however, is worried about the future of the team’s research because last year the UK government withdrew funding from a planned LHCb upgrade. “We are now really scrambling to figure out will we be able to continue doing this sort of research,” he says. Journal Reference: arXiv DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2611.00230

item.title: ‘Show your certificates’ — Amaechi replies Oshiomhole over ‘shallow’ comment
item.description: Sekinat Osundiji Former Rivers State Governor, Rotimi Amaechi, has challenged Senator Adams Oshiomhole to present his academic certificates after the former Edo State governor described him as “shallow”. Amaechi issued the challenge during an interview on Rapid TV while responding to Oshiomhole’s recent criticism of his political positions and credibility. Oshiomhole had described Amaechi as “shallow” and “unreliable”, accusing him of contradicting his previous positions by criticising the All Progressives Congress (APC) and President Bola Tinubu after previously supporting the party. The former APC national chairman also questioned Amaechi’s relationship with former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, recalling that Amaechi had previously challenged Atiku’s emergence as the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) presidential candidate. Reacting, Amaechi said he was disappointed by Oshiomhole’s remarks, insisting that the two men were political equals who served as governors at the same time. “He said I’m shallow, but I hold degrees in Law and Literature, Master’s degrees in both fields, and a certificate from the University of London. I also have a master’s degree from King’s College London, and I’m pursuing a master’s degree in Global Political Economy,” Amaechi said. “Tell him to show his certificate,” he said. The former governor also cited his academic qualifications, including a certificate from the University of London and a master’s degree from King’s College London, challenging Oshiomhole to make his own educational credentials public. Amaechi further recalled that Oshiomhole was among the governors who elected him chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum, questioning why the senator would now describe him as shallow. He said, “He’s not my subordinate. We are equals. He was governor while I was governor. So he’s not my subordinate.” Amaechi also linked Oshiomhole’s criticism to his role in the removal of the former Edo governor as chairman of the APC, alleging that he led the team that worked against his continued leadership of the party. “What is paining Oshiomhole is that he was removed as chairman of the party, and I led the team that removed him as chairman of the party because he was incapable of governing the party,” he said. Oshiomhole had also questioned Amaechi’s credibility by recalling his previous criticism of Atiku, claiming the former Rivers governor once described the primary that produced Atiku as the PDP presidential candidate as fraudulent and challenged his emergence in court. He further alleged that Amaechi changed his position after Atiku approached him to work together. He questioned why the allegations were not raised during or shortly after his tenure as governor. “It took him 12 years. Nigeria has not asked questions. Twelve years to accuse me and falsely. He didn’t say it as I left office, he didn’t say it one year after, two years after, three years after,” Amaechi said. The former governor, however, said he would not respond to Oshiomhole again, adding that he could continue making whatever allegations he wished. item.title: Palace receive double fitness boost ahead of Hoffenheim clash
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Crystal Palace's Quinten Timber (L) and Middlesbrough's Adilson Malanda battle for the ball during the English Carabao Cup third round soccer match between Crystal Palace and Middlesbrough at Selhurst Park. (is associated with: «Palace receive double fitness boost ahead of Hoffenheim clash») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Crystal Palace have been boosted by the returns of Quinten Timber and Jorgen Strand Larsen for the home match against Hoffenheim in the Europa League on Thursday. Midfielder Timber and striker Strand Larsen have been sidelined through injury since Palace’s last European outing, the 2-2 draw away at Besiktas on October 22. Boss Pierre Sage told a pre-match press conference: “Both will be back with us. “They were training with us last week but not ready to play, but now they are ready to play. All the others will be OK.” Palace will attempt to build on their tally of four points from their opening three league phase matches against the Bundesliga side. The showdown under the lights at Selhurst Park will be their eighth game in the space of 25 days, with the Eagles juggling their Premier League and League Cup commitments with Europe. Sage is eager to put their domestic issues to one side after Palace slipped to 18th following three straight defeats. He added: “First of all it’s exciting, because if we play in a European cup, it’s because the team did well last year and won the Conference League. We have to deal with that, but it’s a good thing. “To deal with three different competitions, for the process, it’s always the same because we prepare in the same way. “The difference between the three competitions is the time we have before the games to prepare. “This time we have three sessions before the game, one more than the two before, and that’s really important because we need time to work, especially when we’re in our situation. “What we did during these sessions was really important for the confidence of the players, for their understanding of the game plan and for their capacity to apply it.”

item.title: Cunha avoids sanction for not going straight down tunnel after red
item.description: Manchester United's Matheus Cunha leaves the pitch after being shown a red card during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford. (is associated with: «Cunha avoids sanction for not going straight down tunnel after red») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Matheus Cunha will avoid UEFA punishment for failing to go straight to the dressing room following his late red card in Manchester United’s Champions League win against Roma. Michael Carrick’s Red Devils roared to a much-needed 3-2 comeback victory on Tuesday, when the Brazil international earned a penalty which was converted at the second attempt by Bruno Fernandes. Cunha equalized and then scored a dramatic late winner, with the United forward earning a booking having taken off his shirt in celebration and jumped into the Old Trafford crowd. A second yellow card soon followed for a poor challenge, with the ex-Wolves man then trying to watch the remainder of stoppage time before celebrating with team-mates, when rules state he should have left the field area. United boss Carrick pointed him towards the tunnel and UEFA has confirmed Cunha will serve just the one-match ban at Sporting Lisbon later this month rather than anything more severe. A spokesperson for the governing body said: “The UEFA official reports did not mention anything about this incident. “Therefore the automatic one-match ban following two yellow cards should not be extended for this reason. We are not investigating further this matter.” United livewire Cunha became the first player in Champions League history to win a penalty, score a goal and be sent off in the same match. Head coach Carrick said: “Matheus can do those things, he has those moments. “We put him inside, we swapped him with Bryan (Mbeumo) at half-time to try to get him in the middle of the pitch, to try to give us a little bit of a different shape, putting him in the centre of the pitch. “He found himself in good positions. Disappointed with how it finished but, again, it just shows how much he cares and he’s willing to do, when he’s in that frame of mind and he’s in that mood, that’s why we want him here.”
item.content:encoded: Manchester United's Matheus Cunha leaves the pitch after being shown a red card during the UEFA Champions League soccer match between Manchester United and AS Roma at Old Trafford. (is associated with: «Cunha avoids sanction for not going straight down tunnel after red») Martin Rickett/PA Wire/dpa Matheus Cunha will avoid UEFA punishment for failing to go straight to the dressing room following his late red card in Manchester United’s Champions League win against Roma. Michael Carrick’s Red Devils roared to a much-needed 3-2 comeback victory on Tuesday, when the Brazil international earned a penalty which was converted at the second attempt by Bruno Fernandes. Cunha equalized and then scored a dramatic late winner, with the United forward earning a booking having taken off his shirt in celebration and jumped into the Old Trafford crowd. A second yellow card soon followed for a poor challenge, with the ex-Wolves man then trying to watch the remainder of stoppage time before celebrating with team-mates, when rules state he should have left the field area. United boss Carrick pointed him towards the tunnel and UEFA has confirmed Cunha will serve just the one-match ban at Sporting Lisbon later this month rather than anything more severe. A spokesperson for the governing body said: “The UEFA official reports did not mention anything about this incident. “Therefore the automatic one-match ban following two yellow cards should not be extended for this reason. We are not investigating further this matter.” United livewire Cunha became the first player in Champions League history to win a penalty, score a goal and be sent off in the same match. Head coach Carrick said: “Matheus can do those things, he has those moments. “We put him inside, we swapped him with Bryan (Mbeumo) at half-time to try to get him in the middle of the pitch, to try to give us a little bit of a different shape, putting him in the centre of the pitch. “He found himself in good positions. Disappointed with how it finished but, again, it just shows how much he cares and he’s willing to do, when he’s in that frame of mind and he’s in that mood, that’s why we want him here.”

item.title: Lampard happy with increased output from Coventry’s summer signings
item.description: Lampard happy with increased output from Coventry’s summer signings Frank Lampard says he is pleased with the increased contributions shown by Coventry City’s summer signings. Coventry claimed their third win of the season last weekend against Sunderland , with five summer signings starting, having spent around £130 million on 12 new signings during the summer transfer window. The Sky Blues find themselves in 16th place in their Premier League after nine matches, two points and places above the relegation zone. Ahead of his side’s clash with Everton on Friday night, Lampard spoke of his delight at how his new players have integrated within the established players in the squad. Lampard said: “I would guess my selection so far was probably about three new players, sort of on average, and I think it’s an interesting point because I keep talking about it, but the players that came up [with us], we’re very, very happy with and some of them haven’t played in this league a lot, so they will be learning on their feet a bit. “When we recruited, we wanted to recruit players that could come in and help us, as in start for us, I really pushed to be there because we haven’t got time for development. You can’t get promoted and try and develop too much. “So I think it’s nice that in nine games you’re seeing that now, pretty even push of the new players coming in, understanding what we do, how we train, how we behave, what’s the demands of the team, and some get that quicker than others. “And the players here who live in their own individual cases have never maybe played in the Premier League striving to get there, we have to give them some time. “So I think to come to have five there, I’m not counting those numbers specifically, but I think when you put it that way, I think it’s interesting and it maybe shows that we’re hopefully getting a nice push from everyone to try and make the team.”

item.title: Tinubu Departs Saudi Arabia For Nigeria After Umrah
item.description: President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday departed King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, for Abuja after completing his Umrah (Lesser Hajj) in the holy city of Makkah. According to a statement by the presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, the President’s aircraft took off from the Royal Terminal of the airport at exactly 5:13 p.m. Saudi time. Onanuga said the Deputy Governor of the Makkah Region, Prince Saud bin Mishal bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Nigeria’s Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and the Consul-General, Muazam Ibrahim Nayaya, accompanied the President to the airport. Before his departure, Tinubu held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport. ﻿ The President had earlier led members of the Nigerian delegation in performing the Umrah rites, including the circumambulation of the Holy Ka’abah. Last Sunday, Tinubu was granted the rare privilege of entering the sacred structure, where he and members of his delegation performed the two raka’at prayers. Inside the Holy Ka’abah, the President offered special supplications to Almighty Allah for lasting peace, security, unity and prosperity in Nigeria, while seeking divine guidance, wisdom and strength to continue serving the Nigerian people. He also prayed for Allah’s continued blessings upon Nigeria, its leaders and citizens, expressing hope that the country’s diversity would become a source of strength, national cohesion and shared prosperity. Tinubu held a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace within the airport before departing Saudi Arabia. Onanuga said the President’s visit to Saudi Arabia provided an opportunity for spiritual reflection, thanksgiving and prayers for Nigeria, as well as a renewed commitment to building a peaceful, united and prosperous nation. The statement added that Tinubu expressed profound appreciation to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman for the special courtesies and hospitality extended to him and the Nigerian delegation, particularly the privilege of accessing the Holy Ka’abah to offer prayers. “President Tinubu left the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia with renewed faith, gratitude to Almighty Allah and an unwavering commitment to the Renewed Hope Agenda and the aspiration of building a better Nigeria for all,” the statement said. Those in the President’s entourage included the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, and the governors of Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Borno and Yobe States, among others. The post Tinubu Departs Saudi Arabia For Nigeria After Umrah appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Wilder v Opetaia joins Fury vs Joshua undercard live on Netflix
item.description: Deontay Wilder will fight Jai Opetaia on the undercard for Tyson Fury ’s long-awaited fight with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff. The 31-year-old Opetaia, who is unbeaten in 31 bouts, winning 24 by knockout, will move up from cruiserweight to heavyweight against the former world champion Wilder. Jai Opetaia had previously called out the unbeaten David Benavidez (Getty) Wilder has history with Fury and lost the final two bouts of their trilogy, with the 41-year-old since returning to winning ways by beating Derek Chisora in London in April . Zuffa Boxing champion Opetaia had previously been linked with unbeaten three-weight world champion David Benavidez, although he will instead face Michael Cieslak . Opetaia had previously signed for Dana White ’s Zuffa Boxing, with White involved in the promotion of Fury-Joshua on 11 December. The former heavyweight champions will meet in a contest almost a decade in the making , headlining at Wales’s Principality Stadium and live on Netflix. Fury, 38, and Joshua, 37, are expected to make their ring walks in the early hours of Saturday morning, and now the support bouts have been announced for the Friday evening.

item.title: Gold postbox to honor Manx athlete
item.description: A postbox in Marown has been painted gold in honor of Manx athete Matthew Bostock [BBC] A postbox has been painted gold in celebration of a two-time gold-medalist athlete. Manx-born cyclist Matthew Bostock, from Marown, was crowned world champion in the 40km race at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in August, andwon Men's scratch race at the UCI Track Cycling World Championships in China last month. The idea to honor the 29-year-old with a gold postbox was put to the Isle of Man Post Office by Marown Commissioners. "Matthew is very humble, he doesn't go around shouting about his achievements. We wanted to do this for him, especially on Ballagarey Road, as that is where he grew up and his family lives," said commissioner Alison Lynch. Lynch said the idea came about following a similar accolodate for Peter Kennaugh in Onchan in 2012 following his world record-breaking achievement at the London Olympics. "Onchan requested for a postbox to be painted and they got it... so we spoke to Matthew's family first and got their consent before approaching the Post Office," Lynch said. Matthew Bostock took the final medal of the 2026 Commonwealth Games [BBC] She added that while Bostock and his family had not seen the box yet, his parents were "very proud, extremly happy and grateful" and Bostock was "absolutely over the moon". "He is hoping to be on the island towards the end of November, and we will try to get something arranged at the box," she added. Lynch said having watched Matthew grow up in the parish and reach the heights he had made her extremely proud. "Not just me, everyone on the Isle of Man is proud of his achievements. People wake up early to watch his live races no matter the time difference. He has a huge backing from here all cheering his on," she added. Bostock has been nominateed for the British Cycling National Champion of the Year award for 2026. The winner will be announced next week. item.title: 'Is Republican Party able to pivot away from MAGA movement, or will it sputter forward leaderless?'
item.description: Does an electoral repudiation of Donald Trump also mark the beginning of MAGA’s decline? Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Ian Reifowitz, SUNY Distinguished Professor of Historical Studies at Empire State University, who describes the Republican defeat as “an absolute and complete repudiation” of the president. He connects voters’ economic frustrations with resentment over presidential enrichment, while questioning whether ideological differences between progressive and moderate Democrats proved decisive. Looking towards 2028, Reifowitz identifies a central Republican dilemma: “If JD Vance is the nominee, he can’t run against Donald Trump”, yet Trump himself may refuse to relinquish control of the party.

Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Ian Reifowitz, SUNY Distinguished Professor of Historical Studies at Empire State University, who describes the Republican defeat as “an absolute and complete repudiation” of the president. He connects voters’ economic frustrations with resentment over presidential enrichment, while questioning whether ideological differences between progressive and moderate Democrats proved decisive. Looking towards 2028, Reifowitz identifies a central Republican dilemma: “If JD Vance is the nominee, he can’t run against Donald Trump”, yet Trump himself may refuse to relinquish control of the party.

item.title: Mirassol and Internacional win their matchweek 34 clashes
item.description: Mirassol and Internacional win their matchweek 34 clashes On Tuesday night (3), Internacional and Mirassol secured important results in the battle against relegation in the Brasileirão. Both teams won their matches, earning three points and some breathing room outside the bottom four. At Arena Condá, Mirassol beat Chapecoense 2-1. Kauan opened the scoring for the hosts just 12 minutes into the match, but Reinaldo and Shaylon completed the comeback for Mirassol. The win moved the team from São Paulo state into 12th place with 40 points and confirmed relegation for Chape, who sit bottom of the table with 21 points. Internacional defeated Coritiba 1-0 at Beira-Rio, with Alerrandro scoring in the 90th minute. The result put the team from Rio Grande do Sul outside the relegation zone overnight, but they need other results this round to go their way to stay out of the bottom four. Coritiba remain in 11th place with 42 points. In the opening match of the round on Monday (2), Red Bull Bragantino beat Santos 2-1, leapfrogging them in the standings. Rodinei's own goal and a strike from Wallace Yan gave Bragantino the win, while Philippe Coutinho scored for Santos. Matchweek 34 continues on Wednesday (4), with teams battling to secure top spot and others fighting relegation. At 7:30 p.m., Flamengo face Grêmio at the Maracanã, while Athletico-PR take on Vasco at Arena da Baixada. item.title: Ocon dropped - is it the end of his F1 career?
item.description: Ocon has driven in 198 grands prix since making his debut in 2016 [Getty Images] Esteban Ocon's career as a Formula 1 race driver is over - at least for the foreseeable future - after a falling-out with Haas led to the Frenchman being dropped for the rest of this season. Ocon, 30, was already going to be leaving Haas at the end of the year, with little prospect of finding a seat on the grid next season. But the acrimonious turn of events in Mexico City last weekend brought that forward by a few races. Ocon now faces a year on the sidelines, with the aim of finding a berth as a reserve driver, as he seeks to rebuild his career. This is not the first time he has found himself in this situation. Ocon was also without a seat in 2019 when he lost his drive at what had been called the Force India team after it was bought by Canadian billionaire Lawrence Stroll, who put his son Lance in Ocon's car. This, though, feels like it has more potential finality about it. Not least because 10 years into his career in F1, Ocon is well known within the sport, both his competitive level and his approach. He's been around the block a few times. His career has not been especially stellar. He has a reputation for falling out with teams and team-mates. And there is a new generation breaking through in F1, led by new world champion Kimi Antonelli. Ocon dropped by Haas for rest of season after row Ocon denies reports of physical altercation behind dropping Rows with his team The catalyst for Ocon's departure from Haas was a falling-out with team principal Ayao Komatsu after Friday practice in Mexico City last weekend. Exactly what led to him being dropped is unknown. No-one is talking, not even off the record, and lawyers are now involved. What is known is that Ocon objected over the team radio while in the car to being told by his engineer Laura Mueller that they were switching his run plan from using soft tyres for his race-simulation run to mediums. Ocon said to Mueller: "No, no. I wanted the soft. Don't do that to me. Come on." It seems the argument carried on after the session with Komatsu. The announcement that he was dropped for the weekend came on Saturday morning. Later that day, Ocon put out a statement on social media admitting "a difference in viewpoints led to a discussion with the parties involved" but adding that he "categorically rejected any reports or allegations suggesting that any form of physical violence was used to resolve any differences of any nature". That followed a report in France's L'Equipe newspaper saying a meeting between Komatsu and Ocon "ended abruptly, perhaps even physically". Haas said nothing more over the weekend in Mexico but on Tuesday evening put out what was already being seen as the inevitable announcement that he would not drive for the team again. Ocon secured a rare podium finish in Brazil in 2024 for Alpine [Getty Images] Complaints and clashes with team-mates Haas had already run out of patience with Ocon long before Mexi

And there is a new generation breaking through in F1, led by new world champion Kimi Antonelli. Ocon dropped by Haas for rest of season after row Ocon denies reports of physical altercation behind dropping Rows with his team The catalyst for Ocon's departure from Haas was a falling-out with team principal Ayao Komatsu after Friday practice in Mexico City last weekend. Exactly what led to him being dropped is unknown. No-one is talking, not even off the record, and lawyers are now involved. What is known is that Ocon objected over the team radio while in the car to being told by his engineer Laura Mueller that they were switching his run plan from using soft tyres for his race-simulation run to mediums. Ocon said to Mueller: "No, no. I wanted the soft. Don't do that to me. Come on." It seems the argument carried on after the session with Komatsu. The announcement that he was dropped for the weekend came on Saturday morning. Later that day, Ocon put out a statement on social media admitting "a difference in viewpoints led to a discussion with the parties involved" but adding that he "categorically rejected any reports or allegations suggesting that any form of physical violence was used to resolve any differences of any nature". That followed a report in France's L'Equipe newspaper saying a meeting between Komatsu and Ocon "ended abruptly, perhaps even physically". Haas said nothing more over the weekend in Mexico but on Tuesday evening put out what was already being seen as the inevitable announcement that he would not drive for the team again. Ocon secured a rare podium finish in Brazil in 2024 for Alpine [Getty Images] Complaints and clashes with team-mates Haas had already run out of patience with Ocon long before Mexico City but whatever happened there was serious enough that Komatsu felt the relationship had to end on the spot. The decline of Ocon's time with Haas has echoes of previous experiences. Ocon has been beaten by team-mate Oliver Bearman over his two seasons at Haas, just as he was outpaced by Pierre Gasly and before him Fernando Alonso at Alpine, and Daniel Ricciardo before that when the team was known as Renault. When Haas signed Ocon, his reputation was such that many were surprised they had taken him. Komatsu felt he could make it work. But the team began to notice a pattern. When Ocon was struggling, he would become defensive and blame the team and car. Tensions would rise and the team felt there was a lack of accountability from the driver. There were also clashes with his team-mate, for example in Monaco practice when they got in each other's way and Bearman ended up calling Ocon "an idiot" over the radio. They also crashed into each other towards the end of the British Grand Prix last year. Competitive tensions between team-mates are common in F1. A driver's team-mate is also their biggest rival - the only person with the same equipment so the only driver against which they can be directly measured. The parallel need to work together to benefit the team's overall prospects can be an uncomfortable ask in such circumstances. It's a problem that is causing tension at Ferrari between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc, for example, as was also seen in Mexico. But over the years, Ocon has built an unenviable reputation for both these sides of his character. To outsiders, this can be surprising because he is charm personified with the media, a delight to deal with. He and Gasly - who were childhood friends before falling out nearly 20 years ago - crashed twice together at Alpine. At the end of their two seasons together, was the first occasion on which Ocon was released before the end of the season, dropped with one race to go. Alonso and Ocon also fell out and the Spanish icon did not trouble to hide his distaste for his team-mate's behaviour at times. Ocon also had on-track clashes and team radio disputes with Sergio Perez when at Force India. Alpine also saw the same pattern as did Haas more recently in terms of self-awareness and accountability. Alonso put in a starring performance in wet qualifying in Canada in 2022 and stuck his midfield Alpine on the front row alongside Max Verstappen's Red Bull. That lap was 1.6 seconds faster than Ocon's and team insiders say he simply could not accept that he had been that much slower. Ocon is said to have insisted there must have been something wrong with his car and continued to do so for several races. The team checked and checked and there was nothing wrong. It was just Alonso doing what great drivers sometimes do and redefining perceptions of what was possible. All drivers complain. It's part of their make-up. Their motivation comes from believing they can be the best and finding weaknesses in the car and improving them is their job and how they make themselves and the team more competitive. The better they are, the more acceptable that complaining is. Verstappen, for example, is constantly having a go about clunky gearshifts or a balance he does not like. Red Bull accept it because he delivers on track at such a high level on such a consistent basis. Ocon's issue is that there is a different pattern. On average, he has been slower than Bearman these last two years, just as he was against Gasly from 2023-24, against Alonso from '21-22 and against Ricciardo in 2020. Finding a way back on to the grid won't be easy Ocon is managed by Mercedes and came through their young driver programme. When he lost his Force India seat, it was Mercedes that took him on as reserve driver in 2019. At one point, team principal Toto Wolff was considering putting Ocon in the race team alongside Hamilton. One of the reasons he did not was he thought their characters would clash, that the relationship would be too combustible. Valtteri Bottas was retained for 2020 after all. At the same time, George Russell, the next Mercedes protege, was excelling for Williams and Mercedes concluded from the data they had on both that Russell was their guy for the future, not Ocon. That was effectively the end of Ocon's career as a potential candidate for a top team but Mercedes helped him back on to the grid with a drive at Renault in 2020, before the team was rebranded Alpine in 2021. It was for them that Ocon took his sole victory, at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix. He drove well but the win owed a substantial amount to fortune. The start was wet and there was a multi-car pile-up that took out Bottas and both Red Bulls. Ocon came out of that pile-up running second to Hamilton. The race was red-flagged. By the time it was restarted, the track was drying. At the end of the formation lap, every single car pitted for dry-weather slick tyres bar Hamilton, wh

item.title: Amorim opens up about ‘biggest’ Milan problem
item.description: Amorim opens up about ‘biggest’ Milan problem Ruben Amorim wants to see his players ‘push the opponents inside their box’ and ‘keep the ball there’ as he admits: ‘That’s the biggest problem with us.’ Milan host Ferencvaros in the Europa League Round 4 on Thursday. The Rossoneri have been inconsistent this season, but won their most recent league game against city rivals Inter, which gave them a massive confidence boost. Amorim: Milan ‘lack the ability to push opponents near their box’ SALZBURG, AUSTRIA – OCTOBER 15: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan, is interviewed before the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between FC Salzburg and AC Milan at Stadion Salzburg on October 15, 2026 in Salzburg, Austria. (Photo by Jasmin Walter/Getty Images) Milan sit fifth in the Serie A table and have lost only once in ten Serie A games. However, their record in Europe is much worse: one win and two defeats. During the match against Inter, they surely showed improvements, but when a reporter asked Amorim how close this team is to the identity he wants to see, he replied: “You guys are always asking about when we’ll reach the top. Even if we win every game, we’ll never feel like we’ve reached the top. We need to improve and improve. “We already have an identity. We want to dominate games. Sometimes we are able, sometimes we aren’t. But in most games, we try to be really positive. Sometimes we change our system or how we defend. Our identity is about being positive and dominant in the game. We clearly lack the ability to push opponents near their box and keep the ball there to create more chances. That’s the biggest problem with us. And be more consistent during the games, and in many games. I think we are getting better at that. I think we are playing better for a longer time, we are controlling the games a bit better, but if I look at the team, we have so much to do. Especially in the final third, we are not getting the ball there and staying there for long. We need time to work on this and I need to help my players to play better in that moment.” MILAN, ITALY – AUGUST 28: Ruben Amorim, Head Coach of AC Milan, reacts during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Venezia FC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on August 28, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Amorim spoke to reporters during a pre-match press conference on Wednesday , joined by defender Koni De Winter, a regular starter for the Rossoneri this season. “Inter is in the past. Let’s prove tomorrow that we can defend even better,” Amorim continued. “We controlled the game well because we had more possession. It’s not about thinking about defending. We defended with the ball and that helps us to think more clearly when we don’t have the ball. Then, I think we were better in the details. item.title: Ex-Celtics Forward Finds New Home Overseas With Former NBA All-Star
item.description: Ex-Celtics Forward Finds New Home Overseas With Former NBA All-Star originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Chris Boucher is heading overseas. The Chinese Basketball Association announced that the former Boston Celtics forward is joining the Shanghai Sharks. The 33-year-old is reportedly replacing three-time NBA champion JaVale McGee in Shanghai and will team up with former NBA All-Star D'Angelo Russell. Boucher went undrafted in 2017 after playing at New Mexico Junior College, Northwest College and Oregon. He started his NBA career with the Golden State Warriors, winning an NBA championship in 2018, before joining the Toronto Raptors. Boucher's best NBA season came in 2020-21, when he averaged 13.6 points, 6.7 rebounds and 1.9 blocks per game. He finished eighth in Sixth Man of the Year voting. Boucher also made history with the Raptors 905 in 2018-19, becoming the first player to win both G League MVP and Defensive Player of the Year in the same season. MORE: Ex-NBA Player Calls Celtics The 'Lakers of the East' Boucher spent seven seasons with the Raptors and helped the franchise win the NBA championship in 2019. He left Toronto in 2025 to sign with the Celtics. Boucher appeared in nine games with the Celtics in 2025-26, averaging 2.3 points and 2.0 rebounds in 10.4 minutes per game. The Celtics traded Boucher to the Utah Jazz at the 2026 trade deadline. The Jazz waived him later that day, making him an unrestricted free agent. Boucher heads overseas with two championship rings and career averages of 8.7 points, 5.1 rebounds and 0.9 blocks per game. item.title: Carlos Baleba injury: Michael Carrick says hamstring problem 'doesn't look great' for Manchester United
item.description: Carlos Baleba injury: Michael Carrick says hamstring problem 'doesn't look great' for Manchester United Michael Carrick has admitted Carlos Baleba 's hamstring injury 'doesn't look great' after the Manchester United midfielder was forced off in Tuesday's 3-2 win over Roma. Baleba pulled up clutching his hamstring just moments after the half-time restart at Old Trafford and appeared to be in tears as he made his way off. Carrick consoled the 22-year-old on the touchline. It is a cruel blow for United's £70million summer signing, who was only making his fifth start for the club. His debut had already been pushed back by an ankle problem he picked up during pre-season with Brighton. Baleba is almost certain to miss Sunday's Premier League visit of Aston Villa. He is also expected to remain at Carrington during the international break so United's medical staff can assess him further. The Cameroonian is set to miss his nation's Africa Cup of Nations qualification double-header with Namibia. Manchester United fears grow as Carrick says Carlos Baleba’s hamstring Injury ‘doesn’t look great’ Carrick stopped short of offering a timeline, but his tone after the game suggested United are bracing themselves for a lengthy absence. "I haven't got any more news on Carlos at this stage," said Carrick. "It's his hamstring, so we'll just have to assess what that looks like. Initially, it doesn't look great. Timelines, I haven't got much more to give you."

item.title: NASCAR Hall of Famer Delivers Blunt Verdict on Martinsville Penalties
item.description: MARTINSVILLE, VIRGINIA - MARCH 29: Bubba Wallace, driver of the #23 Hardee's Toyota, Ross Chastain, driver of the #1 Safety Culture Chevrolet, and Carson Hocevar, driver of the #77 Chili's Ride The 'Dente Chevrolet, race during the NASCAR Cup Series Cook Out 400 at Martinsville Speedway on March 29, 2026 in Martinsville, Virginia. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) Getty Dale Earnhardt Jr. has backed NASCAR’s decision to punish Carson Hocevar and Josh Berry following separate brake-check incidents at Martinsville Speedway. NASCAR fined Hocevar $100,000 and deducted 25 driver points after officials determined he deliberately brake-checked Austin Cindric during the Cup Series race. Berry also received a $50,000 fine and lost 25 points after an incident involving Ryan Blaney. Spire Motorsports went a step further, suspending Hocevar for the next race at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Speaking about the penalties, Earnhardt Jr. said NASCAR made the right decision to prevent brake-checking from becoming a regular part of racing. Although he has a close friendship with Berry, the former driver believes NASCAR needed to establish a clear rule against the practice. Dale Earnhardt Jr. Backs NASCAR Penalties for Brake-Checking The Martinsville incidents happened late in the race and affected two drivers’ results. Hocevar, who drives for Spire Motorsports, repeatedly brake-checked Cindric over two laps. NASCAR reviewed SMT data and determined the actions were intentional. The incident ended Cindric’s strong run. Berry’s incident involved Blaney. After making contact with the Team Penske driver, Berry lost control and brake-checked Blaney, damaging the front of Blaney’s car and sending him spinning. Berry has maintained that he did not deliberately brake-check Blaney and was only trying to regain control of his car. NASCAR responded with separate penalties. Hocevar received a $100,000 fine and a 25-point deduction, while Berry received a $50,000 fine and the same points penalty. Earnhardt Jr. admitted his friendship with Berry made it hard to criticize him, but he supported NASCAR’s decision. “And so look, man, you know, Josh is my buddy,” Earnhardt Jr. said. “It’s hard for me to like, go at him. He’s my buddy. I’m a human being. I can admit that, you know, it’s hard for me to criticize him.” However, he said NASCAR needed to act to prevent similar incidents. “As a series owner, this is the right thing to do for NASCAR. They have to get in front of this.” Earnhardt Jr. Wants NASCAR to Address Brake-Checking Beyond supporting the fines, Earnhardt Jr. believes NASCAR should consider changes to the rear bumper of its cars. He suggested making the back of the car softer to reduce the impact of brake-checking and the damage caused when cars hit the wall backward. “They also need to work on the back bumper of the car and not make it such an anvil comparable to the nose of the car, but don’t stiffen the front back up. Let’s soften the back of the car up,” he said. Ear
item.content:encoded: MARTINSVILLE, VIRGINIA - MARCH 29: Bubba Wallace, driver of the #23 Hardee's Toyota, Ross Chastain, driver of the #1 Safety Culture Chevrolet, and Carson Hocevar, driver of the #77 Chili's Ride The 'Dente Chevrolet, race during the NASCAR Cup Series Cook Out 400 at Martinsville Speedway on March 29, 2026 in Martinsville, Virginia. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) Getty Dale Earnhardt Jr. has backed NASCAR’s decision to punish Carson Hocevar and Josh Berry following separate brake-check incidents at Martinsville Speedway. NASCAR fined Hocevar $100,000 and deducted 25 driver points after officials determined he deliberately brake-checked Austin Cindric during the Cup Series race. Berry also received a $50,000 fine and lost 25 points after an incident involving Ryan Blaney. Spire Motorsports went a step further, suspending Hocevar for the next race at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Speaking about the penalties, Earnhardt Jr. said NASCAR made the right decision to prevent brake-checking from becoming a regular part of racing. Although he has a close friendship with Berry, the former driver believes NASCAR needed to establish a clear rule against the practice. Dale Earnhardt Jr. Backs NASCAR Penalties for Brake-Checking The Martinsville incidents happened late in the race and affected two drivers’ results. Hocevar, who drives for Spire Motorsports, repeatedly brake-checked Cindric over two laps. NASCAR reviewed SMT data and determined the actions were intentional. The incident ended Cindric’s strong run. Berry’s incident involved Blaney. After making contact with the Team Penske driver, Berry lost control and brake-checked Blaney, damaging the front of Blaney’s car and sending him spinning. Berry has maintained that he did not deliberately brake-check Blaney and was only trying to regain control of his car. NASCAR responded with separate penalties. Hocevar received a $100,000 fine and a 25-point deduction, while Berry received a $50,000 fine and the same points penalty. Earnhardt Jr. admitted his friendship with Berry made it hard to criticize him, but he supported NASCAR’s decision. “And so look, man, you know, Josh is my buddy,” Earnhardt Jr. said. “It’s hard for me to like, go at him. He’s my buddy. I’m a human being. I can admit that, you know, it’s hard for me to criticize him.” However, he said NASCAR needed to act to prevent similar incidents. “As a series owner, this is the right thing to do for NASCAR. They have to get in front of this.” Earnhardt Jr. Wants NASCAR to Address Brake-Checking Beyond supporting the fines, Earnhardt Jr. believes NASCAR should consider changes to the rear bumper of its cars. He suggested making the back of the car softer to reduce the impact of brake-checking and the damage caused when cars hit the wall backward. “They also need to work on the back bumper of the car and not make it such an anvil comparable to the nose of the car, but don’t stiffen the front back up. Let’s soften the back of the car up,” he said. Earnhardt Jr. also explained why he believes NASCAR needed to punish both drivers. “I like it because it sets a precedent and a strong tone going forward that this won’t be tolerated. I’m proud of NASCAR, honestly.” He added that leaving the incidents unpunished could encourage similar behavior from other drivers. “I do think that we don’t need this particular type of activity to go unpunished. It will just carry over, and it will continue.” Earnhardt Jr. believes NASCAR has now made its expectations clear to drivers. “They have taken themselves out of that conversation. They laid down the rule. This is the expectation going forward. No bullshit. Don’t do it.” NASCAR Suspension Adds Pressure on Carson Hocevar Earnhardt Jr. also addressed Spire Motorsports’ decision to suspend Hocevar for the Homestead-Miami race. He acknowledged that suspending a driver is difficult for any team owner, particularly when the organization has to deal with the public attention surrounding the decision. “And not an easy decision for Spire to make,” he said. “This is not something that Jeff Dickerson wants to be doing. He doesn’t want to suspend his driver. No team wants to have to go, ‘Hey man, guess what? We’ve got to craft up an announcement that we’re suspending our driver.’” Earnhardt Jr. described the situation as embarrassing for the team and said Hocevar’s response would be important. “This is a big deal, and we’ll see how Carson responds.” However, he believes the full impact of the suspension and NASCAR’s penalty will only become clear next season. “The only thing is we have to wait till February of next year to truly see what difference this may make in what type of race car driver Carson Hocevar is.” NASCAR’s penalties have established a clear warning against brake-checking, while Hocevar’s suspension adds another consequence following the Martinsville incidents. Asked about the goalkeeper's chances of recovering, Gasperini remained noncommittal: “ I don't know, we'll see .” According to ForzaRoma.info , a decision will be made in the coming days. If he misses out again, Vasquez will get another chance after making his Roma debut against United. His performance was largely assured, although he bore some responsibility for Cunha's goal. The goalkeeper also saved Bruno Fernandes' penalty before the referee intervened. While Roma await the return of Gollini and, above all, Svilar, he could once again be the man between the posts. Lazio: Lotito targets FIGC return Claudio Lotito wants to return to a role within the FIGC. According to Adnkronos , the Lazio president personally visited the Italian Football Federation's headquarters this morning to formally submit his candidacy for the Federal Council. The Biancocelesti owner, who has been outside the federation's governing bodies since February 3, 2025 , is therefore aiming to return to the upper ranks of Italian football after almost two years away. His decision reportedly does not depend on the outcome of the federation's presidential race between Giovanni Malagò and Adriano Galliani: Lotito is said to be determined to join the Council regardless of who becomes president. Fiorentina face injury crisis ahead of Juventus: three doubts Fiorentina are dealing with several fitness concerns ahead of Sunday evening's clash with Juventus. According to TuttoJuve , the Viola's medical staff will carry out further assessments tomorrow on Ranieri and Atta , both of whom remain doubtful. The coming hours will be crucial in determining whether they can recover in time to make the squad. The situation is more difficult for Pongracic , who is set to miss the clash with the Bianconeri: he is not expected to return until after the league break. There are, however, encouraging signs for Njie , who came off against Sassuolo with thigh discomfort. His condition does not appear to be a major concern. item.title: Army chief lists 28,000 recruitment, 12 divisions as achievements
item.description: ….Shaibu highlights 681 housing units, operational expansion in first year By Kingsley Omonobi The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu, has highlighted the expansion of the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions, the recruitment of 28,000 additional personnel and the provision of 681 housing units as some of his major achievements in his first year in office. Shaibu disclosed this in a goodwill message to officers, soldiers, civilian staff and their families, published on the Nigerian Army’s X handle on Wednesday to mark his first 365 days as Chief of Army Staff. He said the Federal Government’s approval for the expansion of the Army and recruitment of additional personnel represented significant steps towards strengthening its capacity to address the country’s security challenges. “One of the most significant achievements in the past year is the Federal Government’s approval to expand the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions, along with the recruitment of 28,000 additional personnel,” he said. According to him, the expansion is aimed at strengthening territorial coverage, improving operational responsiveness, enhancing the protection of vulnerable communities and providing greater capacity for sustained security operations across the country. The Army chief said his administration had focused on improving operational effectiveness, institutional capacity and professional standards in line with the constitutional responsibilities of the service. He explained that the Army’s transformation agenda was guided by five strategic pillars: Professional Excellence, Robust Administration, Operational Readiness, Strategic Cooperation and Exemplary Leadership. He said the pillars were anchored on a Soldier-First Culture, which prioritises the welfare, motivation, dignity and professional development of personnel. Shaibu commended officers and soldiers serving in various operational theatres, particularly those engaged in operations against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other threats to national security. “I particularly commend our gallant officers and soldiers serving in the various operational theatres, especially those engaged in ongoing operations against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other threats to our national security,” he said. He also paid tribute to personnel who had died in the line of duty, acknowledging their sacrifices in the service of the country. “I acknowledge with profound respect the sacrifices of personnel who have paid the supreme price in the service of our fatherland and honour their memory,” he said. The COAS also extended his appreciation to wounded personnel undergoing recovery and urged all officers and soldiers to maintain professionalism, respect human rights and comply with the rules of engagement while carrying out their duties. He said the Federal Government’s approval for the expansion of the Army and recruitment of additional personnel represented significant steps towards strengthening its capacity to address the country’s security challenges. “One of the most significant achievements in the past year is the Federal Government’s approval to expand the Nigerian Army from eight to 12 divisions, along with the recruitment of 28,000 additional personnel,” he said. According to him, the expansion is aimed at strengthening territorial coverage, improving operational responsiveness, enhancing the protection of vulnerable communities and providing greater capacity for sustained security operations across the country. The Army chief said his administration had focused on improving operational effectiveness, institutional capacity and professional standards in line with the constitutional responsibilities of the service. He explained that the Army’s transformation agenda was guided by five strategic pillars: Professional Excellence, Robust Administration, Operational Readiness, Strategic Cooperation and Exemplary Leadership. He said the pillars were anchored on a Soldier-First Culture, which prioritises the welfare, motivation, dignity and professional development of personnel. Shaibu commended officers and soldiers serving in various operational theatres, particularly those engaged in operations against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other threats to national security. “I particularly commend our gallant officers and soldiers serving in the various operational theatres, especially those engaged in ongoing operations against terrorism, insurgency, banditry and other threats to our national security,” he said. He also paid tribute to personnel who had died in the line of duty, acknowledging their sacrifices in the service of the country. “I acknowledge with profound respect the sacrifices of personnel who have paid the supreme price in the service of our fatherland and honour their memory,” he said. On personnel welfare, Shaibu disclosed that 681 housing units had been delivered under the Affordable Home Ownership Option for All Soldiers Scheme. The units comprise 489 two-bedroom flats and 192 three-bedroom flats. He added that additional accommodation projects were ongoing, while existing facilities across military barracks were being renovated to address the housing needs of personnel. “Furthermore, additional accommodation are being constructed and renovated across our barracks to address the quartering needs of our personnel,” he said. The Army chief also acknowledged the contributions of military families, particularly spouses and children, noting that their sacrifices helped sustain personnel through deployments, frequent relocations and other challenges associated with military service. He stressed that the welfare of personnel and their families remained a command responsibility, urging commanders at all levels to prioritise the well-being of troops under their supervision. Expressing confidence in the Army’s ability to overcome prevailing security challenges, Shaibu said the service would continue to consolidate its gains and strengthen its operational and technological capabilities. “Together, we shall consolidate our gains and advance the transformation of our Army into a more capable, resilient and technologically enabled force,” he said. item.title: French blood banks foil new cyberattack targeting refrigerators
item.description: A cyberattack in France targeted three cold stores containing donated blood samples and plasma, authorities said on Wednesday. The incident – which was unsuccessful due to the facilities' alarm systems – is the latest in a series of suspected attacks that have targeted refrigerators in European supermarkets, as well as French cooperative bank, Credit Mutuel Arkea, which was also affected Wednesday.

item.title: US midterm elections: Gen Z gives Democrats their strongest support
item.description: In the US midterm elections, 50 million members of Gen Z were eligible to vote. Young voters gave Democrats the strongest support, with 75% of them voting for the party. This generation will be the biggest voting bloc in the United States in the coming years. FRANCE 24's Ophelie Jacobson has more.

item.title: Colts Could Trade Daniel Jones to 2 Teams Before NFL Deadline
item.description: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - DECEMBER 07: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on during the first quarter against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium on December 07, 2025 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) Getty MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts looks to pass against the Minnesota Vikings in the first quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) Getty The NFL trade deadline is approaching, and the Indianapolis Colts are clear sellers. One name that hasn’t come up much, at least in the context of being moved by Nov. 10, is quarterback Daniel Jones. Jones is on a two-year, $88 million contract. It can be tough to move that much money in the middle of the season. He’s also clearly the guy Indy wants to keep starting at the moment. They seem to refuse to give a real look to Anthony Richardson, and QB3 Riley Leonard remains in that spot on the depth chart for now. Still, the Colts’ long-term future seems less and less likely to include Jones, whether that’s a move very soon or one in the next year-plus by the end of this two-year contract. And on Wednesday, ESPN’s Adam Schefter dropped a thought on the NFL world. He wondered if the Colts could move Jones before the deadline. Daniel Jones Trade Rumor Getty MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA – OCTOBER 25: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts looks to pass against the Minnesota Vikings in the first quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) On his podcast that he posted on Wednesday morning, Schefter decided to bring up Jones. He had already predicted that both Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs will indeed be traded before Tuesday’s deadline. But then he had this to say: “We’re talking about Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs. But what about Daniel Jones? What about Daniel Jones? I see you turn your head. Hold on (to host Ty Schmit). Could the Baltimore Ravens make a run at Daniel Jones? Could the Minnesota Vikings make a run at Daniel Jones? I know we’re focused in on Taylor and Downs, as we should be, and I’m not telling you they’re trading Daniel Jones. But sometimes it’s the curveball that you don’t see.” It would certainly be a headline-grabbing move if Jones got traded. If the Colts could cash in now, they may have to consider it. Baltimore in particular needs to find quarterback help somewhere with it looking like Lamar Jackson will miss a huge chunk of the rest of the season and potentially the whole rest of the season. item.title: Vikings Coach Floated as Potential Aaron Glenn Replacement for Jets
item.description: (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) Getty The Minnesota Vikings are 6-1, and that’s largely thanks to their defense, led by defensive coordinator Brian Flores. Even in the Week 8 loss to the Detroit Lions, the Vikings’ defense only gave up 19 points despite allowing 230 rushing yards. Even on off days, the Vikings’ defense still gives the team a chance to win games. As a result, regardless of how the overall team finishes this season, could this be enough for Flores to garner head-coaching interest despite his lawsuit with the league ? Former NFL QB Boomer Esiason believes the answer is yes and notes that the New York Jets should be calling Flores to replace head coach Aaron Glenn. Moreover, Esiason states that hiring the Vikings coach could resemble their hiring of Rex Ryan in 2009. “[Flores] would come in here and try to do exactly what Rex Ryan did,” Esiason said in a Nov. 3 video from WFAN . “We’re winning with defense first. I’m getting this thing straightened out. We’ve got enough offensive players. We’re going to get some defensive badasses in here. “We’re going to start playing some defense. I’d like a guy with a chip on his shoulder. Rex came in with a chip on his shoulder. I think Aaron Glenn tried to come in with a chip on his shoulder, but unfortunately, with all the inexperience around him, including Justin Fields at quarterback, they didn’t have a chance.” Brian Flores Could Want to Prove He’s a Head Coach Meanwhile, in the same segment, Gregg Giannotti said that Flores might accept the Jets job on the premise that he gets to face the Miami Dolphins twice a season. Flores compiled a regular-season head coaching record of 24–25 (.490) during his three seasons, including two winning seasons. “[Flores has a] major chip on his shoulder,” Giannotti said. “He wants to prove to everybody that he can win as a head coach. He feels like he’s been passed over many times before. He was in that division and hates the Dolphins.” Vikings DC Brian Flores on Facing Bills’ Josh Allen Speaking of Flores and the AFC East, the Vikings will be facing Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills . Ahead of the Week 9 game, Flores spoke about facing Allen and the challenges that the quarterback brings to an opposing defense. “This is the most, or one of the most, dynamic players in our league,” Flores told reporters on Nov. 3 . “He makes a lot of people miss. He breaks a lot of tackles: Big, strong quarterback, huge arm. There’s risk-reward. Pressuring people all the time, every week, and so that’s certainly our play style. I don’t know if we’re going to go too far away from it, but we’re not going to be reckless. “We’re going to understand that with a guy like this, you can have an unblocked defender, and he can make that guy miss. The rest of the coverage, the rest of the rush, we’ve got to do a great job of working through some extended plays because we’re going to have those. You kind of know that going in. But Josh is one of the best players in our league. This i

item.title: Why Brandon Aiyuk will likely be cut before he makes it to 49ers' facility Friday
item.description: Why Brandon Aiyuk will likely be cut before he makes it to 49ers' facility Friday originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . There was some significant news recently regarding disgruntled San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk. He hired a new agent, Drew Rosenhaus, indicating that he's trying to make a comeback to the NFL. But it won't be easy for Aiyuk to return. He'll need to file for reinstatement from the Reserve/Left Squad list. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , that's exactly what Aiyuk just did on Wednesday. However, despite the news of Aiyuk's push to make an NFL return, with plans to return to the 49ers facility on Friday, the 49ers are likely to cut him before then. Why? Well, the team has made clear they have no plans to keep Aiyuk around. 49ers likely to cut Brandon Aiyuk after WR filed for reinstatement "Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has turned in paperwork to be reinstated, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus," Schefter reports. "Aiyuk, who is currently on San Francisco's Reserve/Left Squad list, will be reporting to the 49ers' training facility Friday afternoon, per Drew Rosenhaus." This is some significant news in the Aiyuk saga. For the first time since their split became evident last season, it appears likely Aiyuk will have a path forward in the NFL. But with the 49ers and Kyle Shanahan making it clear during the offseason that Aiyuk isn't in their plans, even with all of the injury issues at wide receiver, the 49ers are likely to cut him. Fans should expect the 49ers to cut Aiyuk soon, potentially before he even gets a chance to return to the 49ers' training facility. His time with San Francisco is over, even as he tries to make an NFL comeback halfway through the 2026 season. Aiyuk is likely to be cut by the 49ers, as his file for reinstatement will finally move things along with his NFL career.
