item.title: Ogun monarch drags Abiodun to court over suspension
item.description: Seeks reinstatement, injunction against enforcement of suspension order By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Eselu of Iselu Kingdom in Yewa North Local Government Area of Ogun State, Oba Ebenezer Akintunde Akinyemi, has dragged Governor Dapo Abiodun and four other respondents before the Federal High Court in Abeokuta over his suspension by the state government. The monarch is seeking an interim injunction restraining the governor and other respondents from enforcing the suspension order issued on October 20, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the substantive suit. In the suit marked FHC/AB/FHR/148/26, Oba Akinyemi alleged that the state government suspended him without prior notice or giving him an opportunity to respond to the allegations against him. Other respondents are the Ogun State Attorney-General, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, the Nigeria Police Force and the Commissioner of Police, Ogun State. In an ex parte motion dated October 23, 2026, filed before the Abeokuta Judicial Division of the Federal High Court, the monarch asked the court to restrain the respondents, their agents and officers from implementing or giving effect to the suspension letter. He also sought an order restraining the respondents from compelling him to vacate the Eselu Palace, preventing him from presenting himself as the traditional ruler or stopping him from wearing his crown and other royal insignia. Additionally, he asked the court to restrain the respondents from harassing, intimidating, arresting or detaining him, or otherwise interfering with his exercise of the rights and functions of his office. The monarch also wants the court to direct the Commissioner of Police and officers under his command not to take any steps to enforce the suspension pending the determination of the application and the substantive suit. item.content:encoded: Seeks reinstatement, injunction against enforcement of suspension order By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Eselu of Iselu Kingdom in Yewa North Local Government Area of Ogun State, Oba Ebenezer Akintunde Akinyemi, has dragged Governor Dapo Abiodun and four other respondents before the Federal High Court in Abeokuta over his suspension by the state government. The monarch is seeking an interim injunction restraining the governor and other respondents from enforcing the suspension order issued on October 20, 2026, pending the hearing and determination of the substantive suit. In the suit marked FHC/AB/FHR/148/26, Oba Akinyemi alleged that the state government suspended him without prior notice or giving him an opportunity to respond to the allegations against him. Other respondents are the Ogun State Attorney-General, the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, the Nigeria Police Force and the Commissioner of Police, Ogun State. In an ex parte motion dated October 23, 2026, filed before the Abeokuta Judicial Division of the Federal High Court, the monarch asked the court to restrain the respondents, their agents and officers from implementing or giving effect to the suspension letter. He also sought an order restraining the respondents from compelling him to vacate the Eselu Palace, preventing him from presenting himself as the traditional ruler or stopping him from wearing his crown and other royal insignia. Additionally, he asked the court to restrain the respondents from harassing, intimidating, arresting or detaining him, or otherwise interfering with his exercise of the rights and functions of his office. The monarch also wants the court to direct the Commissioner of Police and officers under his command not to take any steps to enforce the suspension pending the determination of the application and the substantive suit. In a 12-paragraph affidavit supporting the application, Oba Akinyemi stated that he received a letter dated October 20, 2026, from the Commissioner for Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs, notifying him of his immediate suspension as the Eselu of Iselu Kingdom. According to him, the letter directed him to vacate the palace immediately, stop presenting himself as the traditional ruler and refrain from wearing or using any royal paraphernalia. He, however, challenged the procedure adopted by the state government, alleging that he was neither given prior notice of the intended suspension nor afforded an opportunity to defend himself against the allegations. In paragraph six of the affidavit, he stated: “That I was never given any prior notice or opportunity to be heard before the suspension was imposed on the allegation alleged.” He argued that the government’s action raised constitutional issues bordering on his right to fair hearing as guaranteed under the 1999 Constitution, as amended. When the matter came up on Wednesday, counsel to the monarch, Dele Fadesere, who appeared alongside two other lawyers, urged the court to grant the interim injunction. Fadesere argued that the application was necessary to protect his client’s fundamental right to fair hearing and prevent what he described as executive recklessness and lawlessness. After hearing the application, Justice Agatha Okeke fixed November 11, 2026, for ruling. Recall that the Ogun State Government announced the immediate suspension of Oba Akinyemi on October 20 over allegations of partisan political activities. In a statement issued by the Governor’s Special Adviser on Media, Kayode Akinmade, the government said the suspension was approved by the State Executive Council pursuant to Section 52(1) of the Ogun State Obas and Chiefs Law, 2021. The government explained that the action was taken pending a detailed investigation into complaints against the monarch, particularly allegations of his involvement in overtly partisan political activities, some of which were reportedly publicised by him. item.title: Hurricanes Accomplished Something No Other Team Has Matched
item.description: RALEIGH, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 27: The Carolina Hurricanes celebrate their 2-1 victory over the Boston Bruins at Lenovo Center on October 27, 2026 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) Getty The Carolina Hurricanes struggled through a rare bad outing on Tuesday night against the Predators. But they are still rocking and rolling. Even the best teams will put up forgettable performances. That was the case when the Hurricanes skated into Nashville and lost 4-1 to the Predators. It wasn’t for a lack of effort; the Hurricanes put up 30 shots on goal compared to Nashville’s 20. Carolina has continued a trend that has lasted all season: After 17 games, they remain first in the NHL in average shots for and against per game. Per EdgeHalla, the Hurricanes are edging out the second-place New Jersey Devils with 32.9 shots for compared to Jersey’s 32.7. Carolina’s willingness to take shots at the net is one reason they rank third in the NHL with 64 goals scored. That is good for 3.76 goals per game. The Hurricanes are also edging out the Dallas Stars in shots against per game for the league lead. Dallas has allowed 22.5 shots per contest, while Carolina has allowed 22.3. Allowing just 20 against Nashville on Tuesday night surely helped the cause. Carolina’s Incredible Shots For vs. Shots Against Ratio Has Paid Dividends It is still early in the season, but this trend continues what drove the Hurricanes to hoisting the Stanley Cup in June. Across 82 games, Carolina finished second in the league behind only the Colorado Avalanche with 2,637 shots for, or 32.1 shots per game. Their 1,962 shots against was the lowest in the NHL. That translates to 23.93 shots allowed per contest. The Hurricanes were the only team in the NHL to allow under 2,000 shots. The Vegas Golden Knights came close, but they allowed approximately 2,000 shots. This isn’t to say Carolina will repeat as Stanley Cup Champions because of their shots-for-vs. shots-against ratio. That would be far-fetched so early in the season. But it shows just how effective the Hurricanes are when they take frequent shots at the net and allow so few of them. The Hurricanes Must Keep Playing Their Brand Of Hockey A mediocre Predators team tripped up the Hurricanes and delivered Carolina its third regulation loss this season. But that doesn’t mean the Hurricanes need to reinvent the wheel after one bad outing. This is also a team that found a way to lose against the rebuilding Calgary Flames before it went on to win five of its next six games, losing only in a shootout against the mighty Edmonton Oilers . The Hurricanes also posted shutout wins against the St. Louis Blues and Winnipeg Jets in that span. If there are two things the Hurricanes can’t do, it’s to play down to their competition. They face a solid New York Islanders team before squaring off with the Chicago Blackhawks and a double-header in Finland against the Seattle Kraken . None of the above match the Hurricanes. Give

item.title: Palmer should have been sent off for Fernandes barge - panel
item.description: Cole Palmer would have been suspended for three matches had he received a straight red card [Getty Images] Cole Palmer should have received a straight red card for violent conduct in Chelsea's 2-0 loss to Tottenham Hotspur, the Premier League Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel has ruled. The England international was cautioned by referee Chris Kavanagh in the 70th minute after barging into Spurs midfielder Mateus Fernandes. Palmer did so with such force that it caused the Portugal international's head to snap back. The KMI Panel voted 3:2 that Kavanagh should have shown a red card on the field. However, the KMI Panel unanimously supported the decision of the VAR, John Brooks, not to intervene. The majority of the five members of the KMI Panel felt it was "clear contact to the head as well as unnecessary, dangerous and made with excessive force". Two panellists viewed the action as "aggressive with no excessive force", supporting the booking. Palmer was sent off for a second yellow card in the 80th minute for a foul on Jan Paul van Hecke, which the KMI Panel supported 4:1. The midfielder received a one-match ban for his dismissal, missing the Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool. Had he been sent off for violent conduct, he would also have been suspended for Saturday's 2-0 victory over Manchester United, in which he scored a penalty, and this weekend's trip to Sunderland.

item.title: NFL Issues Request Involving Kansas City Chiefs Rookie
item.description: NFL fans witnessed some big performances from rookies in Week 8. One of them is from Kansas City Chiefs running back Emmett Johnson during the 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos. The league issued a request involving the 23-year-old on Tuesday. He led the receiving corps despite being a backfield player. Johnson finished with five receptions on five targets for 128 yards and one touchdown. It was his first score of the season, along with 20 rushes for 77 yards. Johnson’s breakout game is a bright spot as Kansas City dropped its second straight game after starting the campaign 5-0. Johnson is the team’s No. 161 pick in the fifth round after starring for the Nebraska Cornhuskers. He plays mostly behind Kenneth Walker III but may have earned more targets, especially after showcasing his skill set as a receiver. Kansas City Chiefs running back Emmett Johnson (10) looks on during warmups prior to the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Arrowhead Stadium. NFL Asks Fans To Vote For Award Involving Kansas City Chiefs Rookie Johnson is one of four players vying for the Rookie of the Week award. The other finalists are the Las Vegas Raiders’ Mike Washington Jr., the Broncos’ Jonah Coleman and the Los Angeles Rams’ Wesley Bailey. “Who should be the @pepsi Rookie of the Week for Week 8? Vote in the poll below!” the NFL wrote. View this post on Instagram A post shared by NFL (@nfl) The league announces the winner every Thursday via its social media accounts. Fan voting closes on the same day at 11 a.m. ET. The Kansas City Chiefs will play their next game at home on Sunday. They have a chance to snap their skid and get back to their winning ways versus the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. It won’t be easy as the visitors are on a three-game winning streak, but fans at Arrowhead Stadium will cheer the team loudly. A road game follows in Week 10 versus the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. item.title: Capcom Officially Reveals Dragon’s Dogma 2's Next Collaboration: Delicious in Dungeon
item.description: Dragon's Dogma 2 and Delicious in Dungeon have a lot in common beyond just having alliterative names that evoke Dungeons & Dragons . Capcom's action RPG and the delightful fantasy anime about adventurers cooking monsters both revel in the quiet moments of the typical adventure story. Since Capcom released Dragon's Dogma 2 in 2024, I've been shouting about how the two are perfect companion pieces. Now, we're finally getting a collaborative event that officially brings them together.

item.title: Heisman Watch: Will Julian Sayin's injury ultimately derail Jeremiah Smith's Heisman hopes?
item.description: Could the player who has the biggest impact in the Heisman Trophy race over the final month of the season be someone who isn't in the running for the award? Over the first eight weeks of the season, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith was the clear favorite for the Heisman. It was easy to see why. Smith was dominant and setting Big Ten records on a near-weekly basis. But Ohio State quarterback Julian Sayin's injury against Indiana could have changed the whole trajectory of the Heisman race. Smith was still the betting favorite after Ohio State's bye week and ahead of Week 9. But after the Buckeyes lost 30-18 to USC , Smith's odds got a lot longer. Entering Week 10, Miami QB Darian Mensah is the Heisman favorite at +110. Smith, who had better than even-money odds to win the Heisman just a couple weeks ago, is at +275 and just ahead of Miami WR Malachi Toney at +325. No other player has odds better than 12-1. The shift has come even as Smith showed he was still the best player on the field in Los Angeles. He had 10 catches for 83 yards and a touchdown, setting the Big Ten record for career receiving TDs in the process. But it was also his third straight game under 100 yards receiving after erupting for 23 catches for 423 yards across games against Illinois and Iowa in Weeks 4 and 5. Ohio State WR Jeremiah Smith has 62 catches for 1,067 yards and 13 touchdowns this season. Erick W. Rasco via Getty Images The game against USC was the first start for Ohio State freshman QB Luke Fahey. And he clearly understood that getting the ball in Smith's hands was his best chance of passing success. While Smith had 10 catches, no other Ohio State player had more than two among Fahey's other 11 completions. The sample size is limited, but excellent overall quarterback play has been a significant factor for the two Heisman-winning players who have played receiver this century. In 2024, Travis Hunter won the Heisman because he could play both cornerback and wide receiver at a high level. But he also put up No. 1 receiver stats while catching passes from Shedeur Sanders. The QB finished eighth in the Heisman voting. Four years earlier, Alabama's DeVonta Smith was the most dominant offensive player in college football. And as Smith caught 117 passes for 1,856 yards, QB Mac Jones set the FBS completion percentage record and finished third in the voting. Heck, even if you want to go back to 1991 and Desmond Howard's win, Michigan QB Elvis Grbac completed two-thirds of his passes and led the nation in pass efficiency rating. Fahey will make his second start of the season against Oregon on Saturday. The home game in Columbus should provide a friendlier atmosphere — and Smith will assuredly be his focal point. During his Monday news conference, Oregon coach Dan Lanning joked that his defense will try to put 12 players on the field to defend Smith, before remembering how his team beat Ohio State in 2024 with the help of a purposeful penalty for having an extra defender

item.content:encoded: Could the player who has the biggest impact in the Heisman Trophy race over the final month of the season be someone who isn't in the running for the award? Over the first eight weeks of the season, Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith was the clear favorite for the Heisman. It was easy to see why. Entering Week 10, Miami QB Darian Mensah is the Heisman favorite at +110. Smith, who had better than even-money odds to win the Heisman just a couple weeks ago, is at +275 and just ahead of Miami WR Malachi Toney at +325. No other player has odds better than 12-1. But it was also his third straight game under 100 yards receiving after erupting for 23 catches for 423 yards across games against Illinois and Iowa in Weeks 4 and 5. Rasco via Getty Images The game against USC was the first start for Ohio State freshman QB Luke Fahey. And he clearly understood that getting the ball in Smith's hands was his best chance of passing success. While Smith had 10 catches, no other Ohio State player had more than two among Fahey's other 11 completions. The sample size is limited, but excellent overall quarterback play has been a significant factor for the two Heisman-winning players who have played receiver this century. In 2024, Travis Hunter won the Heisman because he could play both cornerback and wide receiver at a high level. But he also put up No. 1 receiver stats while catching passes from Shedeur Sanders. The QB finished eighth in the Heisman voting. Four years earlier, Alabama's DeVonta Smith was the most dominant offensive player in college football. And as Smith caught 117 passes for 1,856 yards, QB Mac Jones set the FBS completion percentage record and finished third in the voting. Heck, even if you want to go back to 1991 and Desmond Howard's win, Michigan QB Elvis Grbac completed two-thirds of his passes and led the nation in pass efficiency rating. Fahey will make his second start of the season against Oregon on Saturday. The home game in Columbus should provide a friendlier atmosphere — and Smith will assuredly be his focal point. During his Monday news conference, Oregon coach Dan Lanning joked that his defense will try to put 12 players on the field to defend Smith, before remembering how his team beat Ohio State in 2024 with the help of a purposeful penalty for having an extra defender on the field. But even if Fahey improves as a passer with every successive game in November, he's got a long way to go to replicate Sayin's production and his connection on the field with Smith. And that gap between quarterbacks could ultimately decide how relevant Smith is in the Heisman discussion as we reach November. Even if Smith keeps stacking up 10-catch games, Heisman voters may become enamored with someone else if he's averaging around 10 yards a catch. Here are the other players to watch in Week 10. Miami QB Darian Mensah and Miami WR Malachi Toney: A case for Smith's continued candidacy despite the quarterback change is the potential vote-splitting that the two Miami stars would need to overcome. But both players have a huge opportunity to separate themselves from the field with a monster game against Notre Dame on Saturday night. Mensah is still completing over 80% of his passes — and on pace to set a college football completion percentage record — while Toney has 73 catches for 1,027 yards and 13 scores across just eight games. Notre Dame QB CJ Carr : Carr, conversely, can make it a four-person Heisman race heading into the final three weeks of the regular season. Since Notre Dame isn't in a conference, Carr won't have the benefit of a conference title game. And the Irish's final three games are against Boston College, SMU and Syracuse. If he has any realistic chance of winning the Heisman, he's going to need to pick apart the Miami defense for the biggest game of his career. Georgia QB Gunner Stockton: As Georgia heads to Ole Miss on Saturday night, Rebels QB Trinidad Chambliss' Heisman odds are at 15-1. Stockton is at 50-1, following just 101 passing yards on 23 attempts in Georgia's win over Florida. Yes, Stockton didn't need to do much in the easy victory. But that performance also came on the heels of his three-turnover game against Auburn. Another pedestrian performance could drop Stockton out of the top 10 at the end of the year. He finished seventh in the voting a season ago.

item.title: USMNT roster: Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie, Folarin Balogun return for Nations League quarterfinals
item.description: Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun and Weston McKennie will return to the U.S. national team for the first time since the World Cup, joining a young squad that roared through four friendlies earlier this fall. Left off the previous roster because they had recently recovered from injuries — and because coach Mauricio Pochettino wanted to take a hard look at young players — the three veterans were among 25 players summoned Wednesday for the two-leg CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals vs. Haiti. Camp will open Monday at the national training center outside Atlanta, followed by matches on Nov. 14 in Miami and Nov. 17 in Cincinnati. It will mark the first activity for the high-profile trio since the World Cup round-of-16 loss to Belgium — a match in which Balogun was allowed to play despite a red card the previous stage against Bosnia and Herzegovina. Pulisic was also in the spotlight that afternoon in Seattle, leaving early with what was later diagnosed as a microfracture of his tibia and fibula. Back at full health last weekend, Pulisic scored the opening goal in AC Milan’s 3-1 victory over rival Inter Milan and Balogun, as a sub, scored his first goal since the World Cup during Monaco’s 3-1 loss to Paris FC. Pochettino invited 19 players who took part in the September-October camp, which featured home victories over Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada. Folarin Balogun, Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie are back on the U.S. men's national team for the first time since the World Cup. Alex Grimm via Getty Images Aside from Pulisic, Balogun and McKennie, the other three additions this month came as a surprise: Nashville’s Reed Baker-Whiting, a 21-year-old left back, and Paderborn’s Santiago Castañeda, a 21-year-old midfielder, were invited to their first senior camp, and Rennes’ Bryan Reynolds, a 25-year-old right back, will seek his first U.S. match appearance since 2023. The senior camp will take place at the same time as the under-23 squad begins the 2028 Olympic build-up with a camp and friendlies overseas. (There is also an under-20 camp taking place at the national training center.) Pochettino had introduced a dozen Olympic-eligible players to senior competition in September-October, and for the Haiti matches, he decided to retain seven of them, including teenage forwards Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall and Justin Ellis. The others are expected to join the junior camps. Roster details will be announced this week. "We are excited to bring this group together at the beginning of our journey in this important competition,” Pochettino said in a written statement. “These players have earned the opportunity to compete and help achieve our main objective, which is to win and advance in the tournament.” Pochettino is expected to speak at length about the roster later Wednesday morning. Folarin Balogun, Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie are back on the U.S. men's national team for the first time since the World Cup. Alex Grimm via Getty Images Aside from Pulisic, Balogun and McKennie, the other three additions this month came as a surprise: Nashville’s Reed Baker-Whiting, a 21-year-old left back, and Paderborn’s Santiago Castañeda, a 21-year-old midfielder, were invited to their first senior camp, and Rennes’ Bryan Reynolds, a 25-year-old right back, will seek his first U.S. match appearance since 2023. The senior camp will take place at the same time as the under-23 squad begins the 2028 Olympic build-up with a camp and friendlies overseas. (There is also an under-20 camp taking place at the national training center.) "We are excited to bring this group together at the beginning of our journey in this important competition,” Pochettino said in a written statement. “These players have earned the opportunity to compete and help achieve our main objective, which is to win and advance in the tournament.” Pochettino is expected to speak at length about the roster later Wednesday morning. The most notable absence among the September-October campers is AC Milan midfielder Yunus Musah. Pochettino also declined to bring back World Cup members such as winger Tim Weah, attacker Brenden Aaronson, center back Mark McKenzie, right back Joe Scally and goalkeeper Matt Turner. World Cup striker Ricardo Pepi wasn’t selected either, and although he had a goal and an assist as a sub for PSV Eindhoven last weekend, he is still working his way back from an injury that cost him a place at the last U.S. camp. Right wing Jack McGlynn, who is in terrific form for Stoke City, was also passed over. A three-time champion, the U.S. has never failed to qualify for the Nations League semifinals since the competition was launched in 2019. The first leg will take place in Miami because of security issues in Haiti. USMNT roster for Nations League quarterfinals Goalkeepers : Matt Freese (New York City FC), Diego Kochen (Lyngby), Brian Schwake (Nashville SC). Defenders : Reed Baker-Whiting (Nashville SC), George Campbell (West Brom), Sergiño Dest (PSV Eindhoven), Alex Freeman (Villarreal), Neil Pierre (Philadelphia Union), Bryan Reynolds (Rennes), Chris Richards (Crystal Palace), Antonee Robinson (Fulham), Auston Trusty (Celtic). Midfielders : Tyler Adams (Bournemouth), Mathis Albert (Borussia Dortmund), Sebastian Berhalter (Middlesbrough), Santiago Castañeda (Paderborn), Weston McKennie (Juventus), Adri Mehmeti (Red Bull New York), Gio Reyna (Strasbourg Alsace), Malik Tillman (Bayer Leverkusen). Forwards : Folarin Balogun (Monaco), Justin Ellis (Orlando City), Julian Hall (Red Bull New York), Christian Pulisic (AC Milan), Cavan Sullivan (Philadelphia Union).

item.title: Packers Could Fix Run Game With $44M Trade Fit
item.description: New Orleans Saints offensive lineman Cesar Ruiz Getty The Rams could bolster the offensive line with a trade Getty The Green Bay Packers are one of the best fits for right guard Cesar Ruiz of the New Orleans Saints at the NFL trade deadline, according to Daniel Popper of The Athletic. Popper notes that Ruiz is a solid run blocker who would fix a huge need that Green Bay currently has. “Ruiz has started 89 games in his NFL career, most of them at right guard, but he also started 26 games at center in college,” wrote Popper. “He missed the Saints’ Week 7 loss to the Steelers with a concussion. Ruiz does not have any guaranteed money on his deal after season. He is functional as a run blocker and pass protector, and he would be an attractive option for a team seeking starting offensive line help.” The Packers started their third different option at right guard in Week 8. Green Bay Packers could trade for New Orleans Saints Right Guard Cesar Ruiz at the NFL trade deadline Getty The Rams could bolster the offensive line with a trade Ruiz is a former first-round pick, going 21st overall by the New Orleans Saints in 2020. Ruiz started in 9 games in his rookie season but has been a primary starter ever since. In his career, he has 89 career starts in his 7 years in the NFL. Overall, he has 5,942 career snaps, with 5,550 of them coming at right guard. He also has 378 snaps at center and 14 snaps at right tackle. Ruiz signed a four -year, $44 million extension with the New Orleans Saints in 2023. While he is signed through the 2027 season, the team acquiring him could release him after the season and not take on any dead cap. The New Orleans Saints are sitting at 2-5 at the bye week, and they could be looking to move on from their longtime right guard for a strong trade offer. Given the Packers’ need at right guard, they could be a fit for Ruiz. Packers Have Big Hole at Right Guard Green Bay was expected to start Anthony Belton at right guard, but he had to shift out to right tackle when Zach Bako-Bewele got injured in Week 2. The team started Jacob Monk for the first three weeks of the season, but Monk ended up getting hurt. After that, they moved to former tackle Travis Glover for the next couple of starts. Glover got hurt, but starting left guard Aaron Banks returned to the lineup, so the team moved left guard Laken Tomlinson over to the right side. The issue is that Laken Tomlinson is a 12-year player in the NFL with just one start in his NFL career at right guard, going back to 2016. His first start in ten years was up and down, but the team was able to get the win. Still, it is hard to think they can continue to lean on Tomlinson. The only case against adding Ruiz would be continuity. If the Saints are listening, Green Bay has to be offering. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Packers Could Fix Run Game With $44M Trade Fit appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Four rising college football coaches who could land a premier job this offseason
item.description: Credit: Marco Garcia-Imagn Images, Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The college football coaching carousel rarely waits for the regular season to end. With openings starting to emerge across the country, successful mid-major coaches could soon find themselves interviewing for jobs that seemed out of reach just weeks ago. Florida State, Maryland and NC State have already entered the market for a new head man, and more vacancies are bound to follow. This will create opportunities for coaches who have proved they can win without the resources of college football’s biggest brands. Four names in particular deserve attention, though their cases are far from identical. Jason Eck-New Mexico Lobos Eck is building one of the season’s most compelling turnaround stories. After leading Idaho to three consecutive FCS playoff appearances, he took over New Mexico and delivered a 9–4 record in 2025. The Lobos are 7-1in 2026, ranked 22nd in the latest AP poll, and have heavily relied on a stifling defense. Eck has shown he can improve a roster quickly without the recruiting advantages enjoyed by major programs. His defensive results and experience coaching offensive lines make him an intriguing long-term program builder. The question is whether he can translate that success against stronger competition. One impressive season doesn’t guarantee readiness for leading a national championship contender, but Eck’s current trajectory makes him worth watching. Spencer Danielson-Boise State Broncos Danielson has already won at a program with meaningful expectations. Boise State went 12–2 and reached the College Football Playoff in 2024, then finished 9–5 in 2025. The Broncos are 7-1 this season and ranked No. 20 in the latest AP poll. Danielson has helped maintain Boise State’s winning tradition through a changing college football landscape. A Power Four school could view him as a coach who understands how to build a winning culture. His next challenge would be proving that success translates to the big stage, where recruiting battles and expectations are different. Lance Taylor-Western Michigan Broncos Taylor’s résumé is still developing. After going 4–8 in his first season in 2023, he led Western Michigan to a 10–4 record and a MAC championship in 2025. The Broncos currently sit at 6-3 on the season. His experience at Notre Dame, Louisville and in the NFL gives him a broader background than his current job might suggest. Still, another strong finish would help strengthen his candidacy. Taylor looks more like a coach building toward a bigger opportunity than an obvious choice for one of the premier openings. Jeff Traylor-UTSA Roadrunners Traylor has the strongest established résumé on this list. Since taking over UTSA in 2020, he has built the Roadrunners into a consistent winner. item.title: USMNT November roster: Three takeaways as Sullivan, Pulisic headline Haiti squad
item.description: For the first time since the World Cup, the U.S. men's national team is set to play competitive matches. On Wednesday, Nov. 4, head coach Mauricio Pochettino named a 25-player roster for the team's two-leg Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal with Haiti. The first leg will take place on Nov. 14 at Nu Stadium in Miami, with the second leg set for TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on Nov. 17. Pochettino has brought back a number of the new faces that starred in the four-match fall window, which saw the USMNT win all four of its first games after the World Cup. But there is also room for a return for some of the team's mainstays, who will look to quickly form bonds with the young players on the roster. Here are three takeaways from the USMNT's November roster. Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall earn another USMNT chance Pochettino gave 13 players their first cap in the last window, many of whom looked ready for the big stage. That has been reflected in the November roster, with eight of those debutants returning: Mathis Albert, Justin Ellis, Julian Hall, Diego Kochen, Adri Mehmeti, Neil Pierre, Brian Schwake and Cavan Sullivan. Sullivan's return was expected, with the teenage star becoming the the youngest USMNT goalscorer ever by scoring in a win over Mexico. Hall's inclusion is deserved after he scored in each of his first three caps, then carried that form into MLS with the Red Bulls. The 18-year-old's call-up is also significant for his international future. If he appears in either game, Hall will be cap-tied to the USMNT and no longer eligible for Poland. Pochettino brought in two new faces for this camp as well: Paderborn midfielder Santiago Castañeda , who is also eligible for Colombia and Nashville SC fullback Reed Baker-Whiting, who has impressed for the MLS Supporters' Shield winners this year. Pulisic, Balogun among mainstays to return Unsurprisingly, there is also room for some of the USMNT's core pieces who were absent from the most recent roster. The headliner is Christian Pulisic, who was omitted last time for reasons Pochettino did not want to elaborate on . But the AC Milan star was always likely to return, and he's now back in form for his club with three goals in his last six games. After a tumultuous summer featuring controversy over his World Cup red card and a failed move to Everton, Folarin Balogun is also back having just scored his first goal since the World Cup. Weston McKennie, who missed the most recent roster with an injury, has also returned after overcoming a minor injury concern with Juventus. Bryan Reynolds sees persistence pay off Perhaps the feel-good story of this roster is Rennes fullback Bryan Reynolds, who is back with the USMNT for the first time since the 2023 Gold Cup. Reynolds moved to Italian giant Roma in 2021 from FC Dallas, but found playing time hard to come by under Jose Mourinho. The one-time top prospect took the long way back to prominence, playing several seasons in Belgium with small clubs Kortrijk and Westerl

But there is also room for a return for some of the team's mainstays, who will look to quickly form bonds with the young players on the roster. Here are three takeaways from the USMNT's November roster. Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall earn another USMNT chance Pochettino gave 13 players their first cap in the last window, many of whom looked ready for the big stage. That has been reflected in the November roster, with eight of those debutants returning: Mathis Albert, Justin Ellis, Julian Hall, Diego Kochen, Adri Mehmeti, Neil Pierre, Brian Schwake and Cavan Sullivan. Sullivan's return was expected, with the teenage star becoming the the youngest USMNT goalscorer ever by scoring in a win over Mexico. Hall's inclusion is deserved after he scored in each of his first three caps, then carried that form into MLS with the Red Bulls. The 18-year-old's call-up is also significant for his international future. If he appears in either game, Hall will be cap-tied to the USMNT and no longer eligible for Poland. Pochettino brought in two new faces for this camp as well: Paderborn midfielder Santiago Castañeda , who is also eligible for Colombia and Nashville SC fullback Reed Baker-Whiting, who has impressed for the MLS Supporters' Shield winners this year. Pulisic, Balogun among mainstays to return Unsurprisingly, there is also room for some of the USMNT's core pieces who were absent from the most recent roster. The headliner is Christian Pulisic, who was omitted last time for reasons Pochettino did not want to elaborate on . But the AC Milan star was always likely to return, and he's now back in form for his club with three goals in his last six games. After a tumultuous summer featuring controversy over his World Cup red card and a failed move to Everton, Folarin Balogun is also back having just scored his first goal since the World Cup. Weston McKennie, who missed the most recent roster with an injury, has also returned after overcoming a minor injury concern with Juventus. Bryan Reynolds sees persistence pay off Perhaps the feel-good story of this roster is Rennes fullback Bryan Reynolds, who is back with the USMNT for the first time since the 2023 Gold Cup. Reynolds moved to Italian giant Roma in 2021 from FC Dallas, but found playing time hard to come by under Jose Mourinho. The one-time top prospect took the long way back to prominence, playing several seasons in Belgium with small clubs Kortrijk and Westerlo. Finally, he earned a move back to a top-five league this summer when he joined Ligue 1 side Rennes. Reynolds has quickly become a key figure for Rennes, which sits fifth in the French table. The fullback leads the team with three assists in all competitions, earning another shot with the USMNT. item.title: All-Pro Linebacker Named Strong Fit to Replace Lions Jack Campbell
item.description: Jordyn Brooks #20 of the Miami Dolphins is once again linked to a Cowboys trade. Getty MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - JULY 30: Jordyn Brooks #20 of the Miami Dolphins warms up during training camp practice at Baptist Health Training Complex on July 30, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) Getty The Detroit Lions are now dealing with the reality that Jack Campbell is not going to be back anytime soon. They already signed K.J. Britt, but that looks more like a special teams addition to replace rookie Jimmy Rolder than a Campbell replacement. So, the team could still be in the mix for linebacker help at the NFL trade deadline. One name to keep an eye on is Miami Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks, according to Daniel Popper of The Athletic. Popper notes that Brooks is on a longer-term deal, which could make him a strong fit. “The Dolphins are executing their tank effectively,” wrote Popper. “They have remained moderately competitive while still losing six of seven games to begin the season. Their rookie class looks promising. The next step would be accruing some more draft capital for 2027. One issue, though, is they do not have many tradable players. Brooks, a reliable veteran off-ball linebacker, is one of the few. He signed a three-year extension in July and has close to $13 million in guaranteed salary in 2027, so any acquiring team would be making a multiyear commitment. The Dolphins would take on $15.6 million in dead money in 2027 if they traded Brooks. This regime, with coach Jeff Hafley and GM Jon-Eric Sullivan, has not been afraid of dead money thus far.” This regime being the group that extended Brooks and his contract for multiple years, might make a trade tougher. The Dolphins clearly value the player and can build around him. Beyond that, giving a team that much control over the contract is valuable. The question would be how desperate the Lions are to upgrade the room after losing Campbell. Detroit Lions Could Trade For Miami Dolphins Linebacker Jordyn Brooks Getty Jordyn Brooks #20 of the Miami Dolphins Brooks is the type of linebacker that Dan Campbell and the Lions would desire. The seven-year veteran plays downhill football and is not afraid to make tackles in the run game. He is not the best in coverage, but Jack Campbell was struggling in coverage this year as well. The big thing would be adding a veteran who can communicate on defense. Brooks has 96 career starts, and the former first-round pick has worn the green dot for the majority of them. He was a first-team All-Pro last year as the leader of the Dolphins defense. There would not be many better leaders that the Lions could add in such a quick time. Lions Have Need at Linebacker The loss of Campbell hurts, but they also lost Jimmy Rolder and were already without veteran Devin White. The room was deep; now there are questions from top to bottom. Joe Bachie will get called up from the practice squad, and Britt will serve on special teams. The room lacks any star power and no real candidate to step in and call plays. Brooks is a great fit. item.title: Leclerc to miss Brazilian GP media duties after daughter’s birth
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Monegasque Formula One driver Charles Leclerc of team Ferrari speaks to the media at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, ahead of the Mexican Formula One Grand Prix on Sunday. (is associated with: «Leclerc to miss Brazilian GP media duties after daughter’s birth») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc will miss media duties ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix following the birth of his first child. The Monégasque driver announced on Instagram that his wife Alexandra gave birth to their daughter Bianca on Tuesday. Leclerc had been scheduled to answer questions from the press on Thursday but has been allowed extra time at home with his family in Monaco. The 29-year-old’s absence means he will not address criticism from team-mate Lewis Hamilton following their tussle in the Mexico Grand Prix last weekend. Hamilton accused Leclerc of working against him after he tried to overtake the British driver during the first lap when the pair were in front, opening the door for Max Verstappen to win the race. “We have to have some serious talks behind the scenes for sure,” said Hamilton. “We don’t have rules of engagement and, whether or not that will change anything from Charles’ side, I don’t know. Something needs to change for sure. “I think it’s a mentality thing. It’s like, ‘Do or die. Either I win or none of us do’, and it shouldn’t be that.” The spat was met with frustration by Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur, who told Sky Sports: “I think it’s just a matter of respect. Honestly, it’s difficult to digest for me to give up a win like this.”

item.title: Zverev debuts as world number one with Paris Masters exit
item.description: German tennis player Alexander Zverev in action agaisnt Italy's Lorenzo Musetti during their their men's singles round of 32 match of the Paris Masters tennis tournament at Plenitude Arena. (is associated with: «Zverev debuts as world number one with Paris Masters exit») Matthieu Mirville/ZUMA Press Wire/dpa Alexander Zverev made his debut as men's world number one with a defeat to Lorenzo Musetti in the second round of the Paris Masters on Wednesday. The German is out of the tournament after a 6-7 (5-7), 2-6 defeat, while Musetti advanced to the third round. Zverev was competing for the first time since taking over the number one spot in the ATP rankings from Jannik Sinner. He will still finish the year at the top position. "It's pretty shocking the level I was able to play in front of Sascha, who was serving really well, especially in the first set," Musetti said in his on-court interview. Zverev was set to take control when he led 5-2 in the first-set tie-break. But Musetti raised his level and reeled off five consecutive points to snatch the opening set. "It was really close. It could have gone both ways. The key was to stay there at 5-2. I played five great points in a row," Musetti said.

item.title: Warriors Get Blunt Kristaps Porzingis Trade News
item.description: Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors Getty SAN FRANCISCO, CALIFORNIA - MARCH 27: Kristaps Porzingis #7 of the Golden State Warriors celebrates with Will Richard #3 after a three-point basket against the Washington Wizards in the first quarter at Chase Center on March 27, 2026 in San Francisco, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Eakin Howard/Getty Images) Getty INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 16: Myles Turner #3 of the Milwaukee Bucks against the Indiana Pacers at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on October 16, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) The Golden State Warriors are looking to move Kristaps Porzingis, and one reporter is not being subtle about it. Jake Fischer of Bleacher Report said Tuesday that the Warriors “certainly do want to move” the center. What Fischer Reported Getty Kristaps Porzingis of the Golden State Warriors. “I can tell you unequivocally from my early outreach around the NBA and to Golden State that the Warriors certainly do want to move Kristaps Porzingis,” Fischer said on a Bleacher Report Live stream. “That is unequivocal.” Fischer described Porzingis as essentially an expiring contract, with only $3 million on the books for next season. He said Golden State is hoping to find a trade partner willing to send back a player now in exchange for salary relief. He also thinks the Warriors landing Lauri Markkanen would be far-fetched. Why Golden State Warriors Want to Move Him Porzingis is out indefinitely, and the Warriors have a thin rotation with Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody sidelined with long-term knee injuries. Porzingis is trade-eligible, so a deal could happen sooner than the February deadline. That does not mean a trade is close. Most teams will not be ready to sell until mid-December, according to Joey Akeley of Sports Illustrated. What a Return Could Look Like Getty Myles Turner of the Milwaukee Bucks . Akeley laid out a few ideas for what the Warriors might target. Porzingis helps another team only if it gets off a long-term salary or receives draft capital, he noted. In theory, the Warriors could build a bigger package around Porzingis and picks for a player like Trey Murphy III . The last time Golden State traded multiple first-round picks was in 2013, for Andre Iguodala , so that route would be a stretch. A likelier path, per Akeley, is taking back a rotation player on a multi-year deal who is not a cornerstone. He pointed to Nicolas Claxton , who is owed $21.1 million in 2027-28, and said a package built on one lightly protected 2027 first-round pick could even aim for Myles Turner . What’s Next for the Golden State Warriors The

He pointed to Nicolas Claxton , who is owed $21.1 million in 2027-28, and said a package built on one lightly protected 2027 first-round pick could even aim for Myles Turner . What’s Next for the Golden State Warriors The Warriors are 5-3 and on a five-game winning streak, so they are not trading from a position of weakness. These are ideas, not reported talks, but Fischer’s report makes one thing clear: Golden State wants to move Porzingis, and it wants help in return. item.title: You voted for the Brewers postseason MVP, and it was a landslide
item.description: Election night brought its share of one-sided results , and that was likewise true when we asked readers to tell us which Brewers player deserved the MVP of the entire run to a World Series championship. With more than 450 votes by the morning of Nov. 4, the clear-cut winner was Aaron Ashby. The relief pitcher garnered 230 of the 456 votes (50.4%), which is a pretty healthy chunk of the vote among nine possible choices. Ashby did something no pitcher has ever done in an MLB postseason before, working 18 relief innings without allowing a single run. Hall of Famer Goose Gossage, whose 1981 Yankees defeated the Milwaukee Brewers en route to an American League pennant, had the previous best relief-pitcher postseason in allowing zero runs over 14⅓ innings. Gossage was on the hill in the eighth inning of ALDS Game 5, when Don Money hit a fly ball that could have given the Brewers a 6-5 lead, but it died on the warning track and was caught by Dave Winfield. The Yankees added two insurance runs in their half of the eighth, and Gossage worked a 1-2-3 ninth in the 7-3 Yankees win. Andrew Miller of Cleveland recorded 16 straight scoreless innings in the 2016 postseason before allowing a home run to Dexter Fowler of the Cubs in Game 4 of the World Series. He ultimately allowed three earned runs in 19⅓ innings. The 28-year-old Ashby twice worked three innings in a postseason game and recorded more than three outs in every other one of his nine playoff appearances save for one. He allowed five hits and three walks but struck out 20 batters. He recorded the final nine outs against the Dodgers in Game 4 of the NLCS , stranding runners at third base with one out on two occasions, to send the Brewers to their first World Series since 1982. In the World Series, he worked 5⅔ innings and allowed just one hit with no walks and nine strikeouts. Ironically, Ashby had struggled in his previous postseason experience, allowing 16 hits, 10 walks and eight earned urns in 9⅓ innings. He had 10 strikeouts. His 30 postseason strikeouts rank fourth in Brewers history behind three other players encountered along the way in the 2026 playoffs: Freddy Peralta (41), Brandon Woodruff (also 41) and Jacob Misiorowski (32). The only other person close to Ashby in votes was catcher William Contreras, the World Series MVP who got 150 (33%). How you voted for Milwaukee Brewers postseason MVP Aaron Ashby, 230 votes (50.4%) William Contreras, 150 votes (32.9%) Jackson Chourio, 27 votes (5.9%) Robert Gasser, 14 votes (3.1%) Cooper Pratt, 9 votes (2.0%) Brice Turang, 9 votes (2.0%) Other, 9 votes (2.0%) Jacob Misiorowski, 5 votes (1.1%) Jake Bauers, 3 votes (0.7%) This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: You voted for the Brewers postseason MVP, and it was a landslide

item.title: How Trump's broken promises on war, inflation handed Democrats the midterms
item.description: Speaking to Fox News following the midterm elections, US President Donald Trump admitted that inflation was likely one reason Republicans did poorly. Many Americans have been frustrated with how the Iran war has pushed up prices, including at the gasoline pump, especially given that Trump had campaigned for his second term on a pledge of “no new wars”, as Ellen Gainsford explains.

item.title: Why the weirdest game of 2026 is also one of my favourites
item.description: Titanium Court is a bizarre world of 8-bit fairies, Shakespeare and surprise songs – its magic lies in never knowing what on earth is going on • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here Earlier this year, I was stuck in hospital for several days, fuzzy on pain medication and bored out of my mind, with nothing but a Steam Deck for company. In the middle of one of those long nights, unable to sleep, I played a game called Titanium Court . It’s a strange creation that looks like it was made for the ZX Spectrum and reads like a postmodern Shakespeare adaptation – a compelling mix of strategy game and match-3 where you rearrange battlefields by matching tiles, before sending tiny lo-fi fairy armies to their deaths. At the end of this late-night run, I met a boss I’d defeated before – a comically hungry dragon – and the game asked if I would like to skip the boss fight and enjoy a musical performance instead. A game has never asked me this before. Of course, I accepted. And then, instead of the familiar tiled battlefield, I was looking at a pixellated singer-songwriter, who launched into an extremely long preamble about the mating habits of the Pacific salmon before saying, “This is a song for anyone else who ever got so horny they could die,” and launching into a soulful acoustic guitar number accompanied by crude images of leaping fish. I began to wonder if my meds were making me hallucinate. Continue reading...

item.title: Students gather to explore Hawaii's glorious night sky | Space photo of the day for Nov. 4, 2026
item.description: null Over 1,400 students gathered in Hawaii to learn about astronomy as part of the annual Journey Through the Universe program. (Image credit: NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/J. Pollard) Students gathered under the stars in Hawaii recently to explore the awesome nature of the night sky together. What is it? From Oct. 19 to Oct. 22, more than 1,400 students on the Big Island of Hawaii gathered for the Journey Through the Universe event to explore astronomy together. The Journey Through the Universe program is currently in its 23rd year. It was originally developed by the National Center for Earth and Space Science Education (NCESSE) and later introduced in Hawaii by the international Gemini Observatory, a program within the U.S. National Science Foundation's NOIRLab (National Optical-Infrared Astronomy Research Laboratory) that works with the Department of Education Hilo-Waiākea. The program aims to introduce students in the Hilo-Waiākea public school system to astronomy as well as the incredible science that happens across Hawaii. The students who participate range from preschoolers to seniors in high school, so the program introduces some students to astronomy and helps others explore possible careers in STEM fields. This year, the program brought in 19 volunteer educators from scientific institutions like Maunakea Observatories and supported hands-on activities and lessons that went from the classroom to under the Milky Way . Why is it incredible? This image shows a growing love for astronomy in progress. From the red glow of a skywatching night (red light doesn't interfere with our ability to see at night like white light does) to the scattered telescopes and students standing under the stars, this scene paints a larger picture. This is just one program, but in bringing together volunteers, educators, scientists and students, the program has created an incredible and enduring learning experience. Whether or not students walk away wanting to pursue a career in STEM, this incredible immersion in astronomy can help to foster a lifelong appreciation for science and nature. It's always a great idea to gather under the stars and explore together.

item.title: Reps pass FCT rent regulation bill amid disagreement
item.description: Lawmakers divided over proposed ban on compulsory multi-year rent payments By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has passed for second reading a bill seeking to regulate rental payments and curb exploitative practices by landlords and estate agents in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), amid disagreements among lawmakers over a proposed ban on compulsory multi-year rent payments. The bill, sponsored by Rep. Paul Sunday Nnamchi, seeks to regulate advance rent payments, arbitrary rent increases and agency fees, as well as establish a unified digital register for housing agents. It also provides safeguards for landlords and tenants, with penalties for violations of its provisions. Leading the debate, Nnamchi said the rising cost of accommodation and excessive demands for advance rent had placed enormous financial pressure on residents, affecting household savings, small businesses and employment mobility. He said the proposed legislation was designed to establish a fairer and more accountable rental system through the regulation of advance payments, reasonable limits on agency fees and proper identification of housing agents. “Mr Speaker, this legislation is not intended to undermine property rights or discourage investment. Rather, it recognises that legitimate commercial interests must coexist with public protection. Landlords deserve reasonable returns. “Agents deserve professional recognition. And tenants deserve fairness and protection from exploitation,” he said. Supporting the bill, Rep. Idris Zacharias, representing Ida/Igalamela/Ibaji/Ofu Federal Constituency of Kogi State, described the proposal as important but called for broader consideration of land administration and housing challenges in the FCT. He also urged the House Committee on FCT and Area Councils to be included in the committee that would consider the bill. Similarly, Rep. Chinedu Ogah, representing Ikwo/Ezza South Federal Constituency of Ebonyi State, backed the proposal, citing the difficulties businesses face in securing office accommodation in Abuja. Ogah said renting a three-bedroom office in Wuse could cost between N25 million and N30 million annually, excluding additional agency charges. He argued that regulating the rental market would provide clearer rules for transactions and encourage investment in the sector. However, Rep. Leko Jafaru Gambo, representing Bogoro/Dass/Tafawa Balewa Federal Constituency of Bauchi State, called for a review of the bill’s title, arguing that the word “prohibit” should be replaced with “regulate”. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: Lawmakers divided over proposed ban on compulsory multi-year rent payments By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has passed for second reading a bill seeking to regulate rental payments and curb exploitative practices by landlords and estate agents in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), amid disagreements among lawmakers over a proposed ban on compulsory multi-year rent payments. The bill, sponsored by Rep. Paul Sunday Nnamchi, seeks to regulate advance rent payments, arbitrary rent increases and agency fees, as well as establish a unified digital register for housing agents. It also provides safeguards for landlords and tenants, with penalties for violations of its provisions. Leading the debate, Nnamchi said the rising cost of accommodation and excessive demands for advance rent had placed enormous financial pressure on residents, affecting household savings, small businesses and employment mobility. He said the proposed legislation was designed to establish a fairer and more accountable rental system through the regulation of advance payments, reasonable limits on agency fees and proper identification of housing agents. “Mr Speaker, this legislation is not intended to undermine property rights or discourage investment. Rather, it recognises that legitimate commercial interests must coexist with public protection. Landlords deserve reasonable returns. “Agents deserve professional recognition. And tenants deserve fairness and protection from exploitation,” he said. Supporting the bill, Rep. Idris Zacharias, representing Ida/Igalamela/Ibaji/Ofu Federal Constituency of Kogi State, described the proposal as important but called for broader consideration of land administration and housing challenges in the FCT. He also urged the House Committee on FCT and Area Councils to be included in the committee that would consider the bill. Similarly, Rep. Chinedu Ogah, representing Ikwo/Ezza South Federal Constituency of Ebonyi State, backed the proposal, citing the difficulties businesses face in securing office accommodation in Abuja. Ogah said renting a three-bedroom office in Wuse could cost between N25 million and N30 million annually, excluding additional agency charges. He argued that regulating the rental market would provide clearer rules for transactions and encourage investment in the sector. However, Rep. Leko Jafaru Gambo, representing Bogoro/Dass/Tafawa Balewa Federal Constituency of Bauchi State, called for a review of the bill’s title, arguing that the word “prohibit” should be replaced with “regulate”. He also suggested that the legislation should have nationwide application, but Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu clarified that its current scope was limited to the FCT. Rep. Ibe Okwara Osonwa, representing Arochukwu/Ohafia Federal Constituency of Abia State, also supported regulation but cautioned against an outright prohibition of multi-year rent arrangements. He disputed claims that agency fees could reach 25 per cent, arguing that they were generally around 10 per cent. On his part, Rep. Ayodeji Alao-Akala, representing Ogbomoso North/South/Orire Federal Constituency of Oyo State, said the bill targeted compulsory multi-year payments rather than preventing landlords from increasing rents. He argued that requiring young couples and other prospective tenants to pay two years’ rent upfront imposed an unreasonable financial burden. “As a youth, when a young couple comes out of service now, and is being asked to pay two years, where will this insurance money come from?” he asked. Alao-Akala said the proposed legislation could provide for monthly, six-monthly or annual rental arrangements while preventing landlords from compelling tenants to pay several years’ rent upfront. However, Rep. Patrick Umoh raised constitutional concerns, particularly over property rights and freedom of trade, urging the House to step down the bill for further consultations and a review of existing tenancy laws in the FCT. Kalu also acknowledged concerns about possible inconsistencies with constitutional provisions, while lawmakers drew attention to Section 44(2)(c) of the Constitution, which addresses laws relating to leases and tenancies. Contributing to the debate, Rep. Wale Raji, representing Epe Federal Constituency of Lagos State, said previous attempts to regulate rents had not sufficiently addressed the problem. He argued that the widening gap between housing demand and supply remained a major driver of rising rental costs. “The bill is not anti-investment. The bill is not against even the landlords or those making investment in the real estate environment or industry. This bill is of good use to both the landlords and the tenants,” he said. The Minority Leader, Rep. Frederick Agbedi, also urged lawmakers to support the proposal, saying the high cost of rent in the FCT was forcing residents into overcrowded and unsuitable accommodation in satellite communities and suburban areas. He said the bill was intended to address excesses in the rental market without discouraging investment in the property sector. The House Leader, Rep. Julius Ihonvbere, described the legislation as important, citing the difficulties Nigerians face in securing accommodation and the activities of unregistered estate agents. “I think this is a very important bill. And I want to thank Professor Nnamchi for thinking about it,” he said. Ihonvbere said the bill would proceed to a public hearing, where Nigerians, professionals and other stakeholders would have the opportunity to make contributions. He urged lawmakers to support the measure, stressing that regulating the sector should not be interpreted as an attempt to discourage property development. “We are in a stage where we have a duty to protect Nigerians. It’s not against you to build your house. You can build as many houses as you want,” he said. In his closing remarks, Kalu cited Section 16 of the Constitution, which provides for the promotion of citizens’ welfare and suitable and adequate shelter. He argued that although Nigeria operates a mixed economy, sectors connected to essential human needs, including housing, require regulation and control. “Not all sectors of the economy should be free and capitalist. Especially when it has to do with shelter, which is fundamental. So, some sectors should be regulated as well as controlled,” he said. The bill was subsequently passed for second reading, paving the way for further legislative consideration and a public hearing to enable stakeholders to make submissions. The post Reps pass FCT rent regulation bill amid disagreement appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Google gives Nigerian health-tech firm $2.5m for maternal care AI
item.description: Project targets 1.9m women in four states By Juliet Umeh Google has awarded Nigerian health technology company, Helium Health, a $2.5 million (about N3.4 billion) grant to deploy artificial intelligence (AI) tools aimed at improving maternal healthcare in Nigeria. The company was the only Nigerian organisation among 15 global recipients selected for the $30 million Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Government Innovation, an initiative supporting organisations using technology to improve public services in partnership with governments. The Nigerian project was unveiled in Lagos during an executive briefing with Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, led by executives of Google and Helium Health. The initiative will be implemented in Lagos, Delta, Kano and Oyo states, with Lagos serving as its primary launchpad. The selected organisations will also participate in a Google.org accelerator programme, where they will receive technical support from Google engineers and artificial intelligence product experts. Speaking on the grant, Helium Health Chief Executive Officer, Dimeji Sofowora, said the company had spent the past decade developing technology and partnerships to improve healthcare delivery across Africa. He said its maternal health initiatives had already reached more than 3.5 million women, adding that the Google.org support would enable the company to expand its interventions and extend access to quality maternal healthcare. “Through our maternal health initiatives, we’ve already reached over 3.5 million women, and Google.org’s support gives us an opportunity to build on that foundation, scale what works, and reach even more women with quality maternal healthcare,” he said. The company’s Head of Public Health, Dr Shona Oluwatola, said the project aims to reach an additional 1.9 million women over three years and contribute to a 30 per cent reduction in maternal mortality. She noted that Nigeria accounts for nearly three in every 10 maternal deaths globally, stressing the need for interventions that would help women identify pregnancy-related risks early and access timely medical attention. “Nigeria accounts for nearly three in every 10 maternal deaths globally. Behind every maternal death is a woman whose family expected her to come home,” Oluwatola said. “Our goal is to reach an additional 1.9 million women over three years and contribute to a 30 per cent reduction in maternal mortality,” she added. The project will deploy Helium Health’s HeliumMum platform to help pregnant women identify potential health risks early and access appropriate medical care. The platform will connect pregnant women with healthcare providers through electronic medical records and AI-powered clinical decision-support tools, while providing governments with data to guide maternal health policies and service delivery. Behind every maternal death is a woman whose family expected her to come home,” Oluwatola said. “Our goal is to reach an additional 1.9 million women over three years and contribute to a 30 per cent reduction in maternal mortality,” she added. Google.org Global Head, Maggie Johnson, said artificial intelligence could significantly improve public services but noted that a gap remained between the technology’s potential and its practical application. She said the grant and technical support from Google’s AI experts would empower the selected organisations to develop solutions to pressing challenges in their communities. “By equipping the 15 selected organisations with funding and pro bono support from Google’s own AI experts, we are empowering the people closest to the problem to show what is truly possible,” she said. Johnson added that the initiative was designed to ensure that artificial intelligence delivers tangible benefits to communities worldwide. item.title: HP Inc hires former GSK boss as CEO
item.description: HP Inc has hired former GSK boss Emma Walmsley to plot its course through choppy PC and print waters. Walmsley spent eight years as the boss at pharma biz GSK and further back in time held various marketing and general management positions at L'Oreal. She has no track record running a tech company, though she was on Microsoft’s board. “Throughout the process, Emma stood out for the strength of her leadership experience across multiple industries, the clarity of her strategic thinking and her ability to translate customer insights into new growth,” said Chip Bergh, chair of HP's board. In the first nine months of HP's fiscal 2026 , revenue had jumped 10 percent year-on-year to $44.5 billion. The print business shrank in that time and PCs generated the growth. However, amid a memory crunch with supplies dwindling, analysts are forecasting PC market contraction in terms of unit sales. Global PC shipments slumped 20 percent in Q3 as DRAM shortages forced up prices and customers opted instead to sweat their assets rather than replace their fleet of computers. Things aren't expected to improve in the final three months of 2026. One beacon of hope for all PC makers was AI, yet many customers aren't buying into the story for various reasons. Walmsley previously said that during her time at the top of GSK she created a "totally different company, in platform, in momentum, in talent, in culture," she told the FT . "I think in time… it will be recognized." She also dealt with activist investor Elliot Management, which operates in the tech industry and called for her to reapply for the CEO role at GSK, claiming her lack of science background was an issue. Walmsley said: " HP is an iconic company with a defining role in shaping the future of work on a global scale. I’m excited to join the team and, together, move forward with clarity and conviction. We will focus on harnessing the power of the AI era and putting HP’s creativity and innovation to work to unlock new sources of growth and deliver lasting value for our customers, shareholders, partners and people." Employees will be crossing their fingers that their new boss doesn’t borrow from the playbook of her predecessor - who hotfooted it to PayPal in February - by running multiple redundancy rounds, and shareholders will hope their stock price show sustainable improvement. item.content:encoded: HP Inc has hired former GSK boss Emma Walmsley to plot its course through choppy PC and print waters. Walmsley spent eight years as the boss at pharma biz GSK and further back in time held various marketing and general management positions at L'Oreal. She has no track record running a tech company, though she was on Microsoft’s board. “Throughout the process, Emma stood out for the strength of her leadership experience across multiple industries, the clarity of her strategic thinking and her ability to translate customer insights into new growth,” said Chip Bergh, chair of HP's board. In the first nine months of HP's fiscal 2026 , revenue had jumped 10 percent year-on-year to $44.5 billion. The print business shrank in that time and PCs generated the growth. However, amid a memory crunch with supplies dwindling, analysts are forecasting PC market contraction in terms of unit sales. Global PC shipments slumped 20 percent in Q3 as DRAM shortages forced up prices and customers opted instead to sweat their assets rather than replace their fleet of computers. We will focus on harnessing the power of the AI era and putting HP’s creativity and innovation to work to unlock new sources of growth and deliver lasting value for our customers, shareholders, partners and people." Employees will be crossing their fingers that their new boss doesn’t borrow from the playbook of her predecessor - who hotfooted it to PayPal in February - by running multiple redundancy rounds, and shareholders will hope their stock price show sustainable improvement. item.title: I’ll end insecurity, hunger, make Nigeria affordable — Atiku, launches campaign
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar, has pledged to tackle insecurity, hunger and the rising cost of living if elected president in the 2027 general elections. Atiku made the pledge on Wednesday in a statement posted on his X platform while announcing the launch of his presidential campaign in Sokoto State. The former Vice-President said Nigerians were tired of hunger, fear and what he described as broken promises, adding that his campaign would offer a plan to address the country’s challenges. “Sokoto, I am here! I am deeply grateful for the rousing welcome as I formally launch my campaign for the presidency from this historic seat of faith, scholarship, and leadership,” he said. He pledged to end insecurity across the country, restore hope to young people and make Nigeria affordable again. “Nigerians are tired of hunger, fear, and broken promises. Today, they have a choice, a plan, and a leader ready to deliver. I will end the insecurity that haunts our communities, restore hope to our young people, and make Nigeria affordable again,” Atiku said. He described the Sokoto campaign launch as the beginning of what he called a journey to rescue Nigeria, urging supporters to unite behind his presidential ambition. “The journey to rescue Nigeria begins here. Together, we will win,” he added. The post I’ll end insecurity, hunger, make Nigeria affordable — Atiku, launches campaign appeared first on Vanguard News .

The news of the partnership comes as part of SpaceX's push to make Starlink Mobile a "major" carrier in the US , competing directly with T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon. The Elon Musk-owned company has already snapped up a swath of spectrum , while recent reports suggested that SpaceX was exploring an acquisition of Boost Mobile . item.title: Senate to suspend bills for new universities in line with FG policy
item.description: The Senate has directed its committees and the Clerk to suspend the processing of bills seeking the establishment of new universities and other tertiary institutions, in line with the Federal Government’s policy. Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, announced the directive during plenary on Wednesday, urging lawmakers to respect the government’s decision to halt the establishment of additional tertiary institutions. Bamidele said the policy was aimed at strengthening existing universities and other institutions before considering the creation of new ones. He urged the Clerk of the Senate to inform lawmakers about the directive and advised relevant committees, particularly those on education, against presenting bills for new institutions for consideration. He acknowledged that lawmakers sometimes found it difficult to reject requests from colleagues seeking support for the establishment of universities and other tertiary institutions. Supporting the directive, Senate President Godswill Akpabio said President Bola Tinubu had discussed the matter with the leadership of the National Assembly and expressed opposition to establishing new universities, polytechnics and other tertiary institutions for the next five to seven years. According to Akpabio, the moratorium would give existing institutions time to develop their infrastructure and commence effective academic operations. He noted that some recently established universities existed largely on paper, with several yet to acquire permanent sites or complete necessary site-clearance processes. The Senate President stressed that establishing a university was a major national responsibility, noting that such institutions should not be created with the same ease as primary schools. He added that universities were national institutions expected to admit students from across the country, regardless of their geographical locations. Akpabio said the Federal Government had made efforts to ensure the geographical spread of universities across the country, making it important to consolidate existing investments. He consequently directed the Clerk to ensure that bills seeking the establishment of new tertiary institutions were no longer listed for consideration. The Senate adjourned plenary until November 10, 2026, at 11 a.m. (NAN) The post Senate to suspend bills for new universities in line with FG policy appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: ADC urges Nigerians to replicate US voters’ revolt against ruling party
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has urged Nigerians to take a cue from American voters by using the 2027 general elections to reject the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, over economic hardship, worsening insecurity and declining living standards. The party said Tuesday’s US midterm elections had demonstrated that no government could take voters for granted, insisting that Nigerians must put their welfare above political loyalty, sentiments and personality politics when deciding who governs them. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC described the American election outcome as a decisive rebuke of the ruling Republican Party’s leadership and economic policies, saying it offered an important lesson for Nigeria’s democracy. “Americans have shown that when politicians become arrogant, when policies punish ordinary people, and when those in power mistake popularity for a permanent licence to govern, the ballot box remains the ultimate instrument of accountability,” the party said. The opposition party said Nigerians had endured years of economic hardship and worsening insecurity under the President Bola Tinubu-led APC administration, questioning why the ruling party should be rewarded with another mandate. “We cannot continue to complain about the cost of living while voting for a President who has made life unaffordable. We cannot demand security while rewarding failure. We cannot earnestly yearn for change while sustaining the very political system responsible for our collective impoverishment,” the ADC said. Urging Nigerians to mobilise ahead of 2027, the party called for massive voter turnout, describing the Permanent Voter Card as an instrument for changing the country’s political direction. “History beckons in 2027. Our voters’ cards must become instruments of change, not souvenirs of citizenship. Nigerians must turn out massively and vote for their own interests,” Abdullahi said. The party also unveiled its campaign message, presenting itself and its candidates as an alternative to the APC-led government. “The ADC and its candidates are offering Nigerians a clear alternative: Make Nigeria Affordable Again. Make Nigeria Safe Again. Give Nigerians Jobs Again,” the statement said. Drawing a direct parallel with the American elections, Abdullahi urged Nigerians to make their votes count in 2027, warning that the APC should not mistake its hold on power for a permanent mandate. “If Americans can use their votes to demand better, Nigerians can do the same. In 2027, let our votes speak louder than the APC-induced suffering,” he said. The post 2027: ADC urges Nigerians to replicate US voters’ revolt against ruling party appeared first on Vanguard News .
